questions.question: What are regulatory signs?
options: Signs that warn motorists of potentially hazardous conditions on the road
Signs that inform road users of traffic laws and regulations which, if disregarded, will constitute an offense
Signs that provide directions and distances to destinations
Signs that mark expressway entrances and exits
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs inform road users of traffic laws and regulations which, if disregarded, will constitute an offense.

questions.question: What must a driver do when approaching a STOP sign?
options: Slow down and proceed if the intersection is clear
Stop at the designated stop line
Yield to vehicles on the left only
questions.explanation: The STOP sign requires the driver to stop at the designated STOP LINE.

questions.question: How far from a STOP sign is parking prohibited?
questions.explanation: No parking is allowed within 6 meters of a STOP sign.

questions.question: What must a driver do when approaching a GIVE WAY sign?
options: Yield to the vehicles on the right side of the intersection
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly
questions.explanation: The GIVE WAY sign requires the driver to yield to vehicles on the right side of the intersection.

questions.question: What type of regulatory sign is the LEFT TURNER MUST GIVE WAY?
questions.explanation: LEFT TURNER MUST GIVE WAY is listed under Priority Signs in the regulatory signs section.

questions.question: Which category includes STOP, GIVE WAY, and LEFT TURNER MUST GIVE WAY signs?
questions.explanation: STOP, GIVE WAY, and LEFT TURNER MUST GIVE WAY are all Priority Signs under Regulatory Signs.

questions.question: What does the VEHICLE MAY PASS EITHER SIDE sign indicate?
options: Vehicles must pass only on the left side
Vehicles must pass only on the right side
Vehicles may pass on either the left or right side
questions.explanation: The VEHICLE MAY PASS EITHER SIDE sign allows vehicles to pass on either side.

questions.question: What type of regulatory sign is VEHICLE MAY PASS EITHER SIDE?
questions.explanation: VEHICLE MAY PASS EITHER SIDE is classified as a Directional Sign under Regulatory Signs.

questions.question: What do directional signs indicate?
options: The maximum speed allowed on a road
The direction or directions in which a motorist is obliged to follow
The distance to the nearest town
questions.explanation: Directional signs indicate the direction(s) in which the motorist is obliged to follow.

questions.question: What does the NO ENTRY FOR ALL TYPES OF VEHICLE sign mean?
options: No vehicle of any type may enter
questions.explanation: NO ENTRY FOR ALL TYPES OF VEHICLE prohibits entry for every type of vehicle.

questions.question: Which sign prohibits entry for bicycles?
options: NO ENTRY FOR ALL TYPES OF VEHICLE
questions.explanation: NO BICYCLES is listed among the specific prohibitive/restrictive signs.

questions.question: What type of vehicle is prohibited by the NO TRICYCLES sign?
questions.explanation: NO TRICYCLES specifically prohibits tricycles from entering the road.

questions.question: What does the NO PEDESTRIAN CROSSING sign indicate?
options: Pedestrians are not allowed to cross the road
Pedestrians may cross only at night
questions.explanation: NO PEDESTRIAN CROSSING means pedestrians are not allowed to cross the road.

questions.question: What does the USING OVERPASS OR USE PED XING sign require?
options: Pedestrians must cross the road at any point
Pedestrians must use an overpass or pedestrian crossing
questions.explanation: The sign instructs pedestrians to use an overpass or pedestrian crossing.

questions.question: What does the NO RIGHT TURN sign indicate?
options: Vehicles are not allowed to turn right
Only trucks are not allowed to turn right
Vehicles may turn right with caution
questions.explanation: The NO RIGHT TURN sign means vehicles are not allowed to turn right.

questions.question: What does the NO LEFT TURN sign indicate?
options: Vehicles are not allowed to turn left
Only buses may not turn left
Vehicles may turn left with caution
questions.explanation: The NO LEFT TURN sign means vehicles are not allowed to turn left.

questions.question: What does the NO U-TURN sign indicate?
options: Vehicles are not allowed to make a U-turn
Only emergency vehicles may make a U-turn
questions.explanation: The NO U-TURN sign means vehicles are not allowed to make a U-turn.

questions.question: What does the NO OVERTAKING ZONE sign indicate?
options: Overtaking is allowed only for buses
Overtaking is prohibited in the designated zone
Overtaking is allowed only at night
questions.explanation: The NO OVERTAKING ZONE sign indicates a zone where overtaking is prohibited.

questions.question: Which regulatory sign subcategory includes NO CARS, NO BUSES, and NO TRUCKS?
questions.explanation: Prohibitive/restrictive signs include signs prohibiting specific vehicle types.

questions.question: Which sign prohibits animal-drawn vehicles?
questions.explanation: NO ANIMAL DRAWN VEHICLES is listed among the specific prohibitive/restrictive signs.

questions.question: Which sign prohibits pushcarts from entering?
questions.explanation: NO PUSHCARTS is listed among the specific prohibitive/restrictive signs.

questions.question: What type of sign is NO ENTRY FOR ALL TYPES OF VEHICLE?
questions.explanation: NO ENTRY signs are classified under Prohibitive/Restrictive Signs.

questions.question: What does a maximum speed restriction sign indicate?
options: The minimum speed a vehicle must maintain
The maximum speed at which vehicles are allowed to travel
The speed limit only for trucks
questions.explanation: Maximum speed restriction signs indicate the highest speed at which vehicles are legally allowed to travel.

questions.question: What does the End of Speed Restrictions sign indicate?
options: A new speed limit begins ahead
The previously posted speed limit no longer applies
questions.explanation: The End of Speed Restrictions sign indicates that the previous speed restriction is terminated.

questions.question: What does a minimum speed restriction sign mean?
options: Vehicles must not exceed the posted speed
Vehicles must travel at or above the posted speed
The speed shown is only a suggestion
questions.explanation: Minimum speed restriction signs require vehicles to maintain at least the posted speed.

questions.question: What does an allowable parking and loading zone sign indicate?
options: Parking is prohibited at all times
Parking and loading are permitted at a given time and place
Loading is prohibited but parking is allowed
questions.explanation: Allowable parking and loading zone signs permit parking and loading at a given time and place.

questions.question: What does the No Stopping Anytime sign indicate?
options: Stopping is allowed only for buses
Stopping is prohibited at any time
Stopping is allowed for five minutes
Stopping is allowed except during rush hour
questions.explanation: The No Stopping Anytime sign means stopping is prohibited at all times.

questions.question: What does a No Loading and Unloading Zone sign mean?
options: Loading is allowed but unloading is not
Both loading and unloading are prohibited in the zone
Only trucks may load and unload
Loading is allowed only at night
questions.explanation: A No Loading and Unloading Zone sign prohibits both loading and unloading.

questions.question: What is the restriction near a fire hydrant sign according to the FDM?
questions.explanation: The Fire Hydrant sign states 'No waiting within 4 meters'. The source uses the term 'waiting'.

questions.question: What does the BUS-PUJ STOP ZONE sign indicate?
options: Parking is allowed for all vehicles
questions.explanation: The BUS-PUJ STOP ZONE sign states that parking is not allowed.

questions.question: What does the BUS STOP ZONE sign indicate?
options: Only buses are allowed to pass through
questions.explanation: The BUS STOP ZONE sign indicates that parking is not allowed.

questions.question: What happens to a vehicle parked in a TOW-AWAY ZONE?
options: The vehicle receives only a warning
The parked vehicle will be towed
The vehicle is allowed to park for 15 minutes
questions.explanation: The TOW-AWAY ZONE sign states that parked vehicles will be towed.

questions.question: What does the PUJ STOP ZONE sign indicate?
questions.explanation: The PUJ STOP ZONE sign states that parking is not allowed.

questions.question: What does the yellow box sign prohibit?
options: No parking anytime from Monday to Friday
No stopping or parking anytime within the yellow box
Parking is allowed only for buses
questions.explanation: No stopping or parking is allowed anytime within the yellow box.

questions.question: When does a No Parking Anytime sign with a Monday to Friday restriction apply?
options: Only during rush hours on weekdays
questions.explanation: No parking is prohibited anytime from Monday to Friday.

questions.question: What does the RIGHT TURNER CROSS AT BROKEN LINES sign allow?
options: Vehicles from the right lane may cross the broken line to turn left
Vehicles from the left lane may cross the broken line to turn right within the BUS/PUJ zone
Vehicles may overtake at the broken line
Vehicles must stop at the broken line
questions.explanation: Vehicles from the left lane may cross the broken line to turn right within the BUS/PUJ zone.

questions.question: What is the gross axle load limit for the restrictive no-entry sign?
questions.explanation: The sign prohibits entry for vehicles with gross axle load of more than 2 tons.

questions.question: What is the gross vehicle mass limit for the restrictive no-entry sign?
questions.explanation: The sign prohibits entry for vehicles with gross vehicle mass of more than 5 tons.

questions.question: What is the length restriction for vehicles on restricted roads?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with more than 10 meters in length are prohibited.

questions.question: What is the width restriction for vehicles on restricted roads?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with more than 2 meters in width are prohibited.

questions.question: What is the height restriction for vehicles on restricted roads?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with more than 3.5 meters in height are prohibited.

questions.question: What does the No Blowing of Horns sign indicate?
options: Horns must be used only at intersections
The use of vehicle horns is prohibited in the area
Horns may be used only during emergencies
Horns must be tested before entering
questions.explanation: The No Blowing of Horns sign prohibits the use of horns in the designated area.

questions.question: Under which Republic Act is the USE SEAT BELT sign mandated?
questions.explanation: The USE SEAT BELT sign is used pursuant to R.A. No. 8750, the Seat Belt Law.

questions.question: Which sign alerts motorists to be aware of a pedestrian crossing?
options: USING OVERPASS OR USE PED XING
questions.explanation: The 'Be aware of pedestrian crossing' sign is a miscellaneous regulatory sign.

questions.question: What does the 'Be aware of children crossing' sign indicate?
options: Motorists must honk at children crossing
Motorists should be alert and cautious for children crossing
Children may cross only at designated times
questions.explanation: The sign warns motorists to be aware of children crossing the road.

questions.question: What does the 'Be aware of Persons with Disabilities crossing' sign indicate?
options: PWDs are not allowed to cross
Motorists should be alert for PWDs crossing the road
Only PWDs may use the crosswalk
A special lane for PWDs is ahead
questions.explanation: The sign alerts motorists to be aware of Persons with Disabilities crossing.

questions.question: What does the 'Bicycle lane ahead' regulatory sign indicate?
options: A bicycle lane is present ahead on the road
Only bicycles may use the road
questions.explanation: The sign alerts motorists to be aware of a bicycle lane ahead.

questions.question: Which regulatory sign subcategory includes the USE SEAT BELT sign?
questions.explanation: The USE SEAT BELT sign is listed under Miscellaneous Signs.

questions.question: What are regulatory signs that set speed limits called?
questions.explanation: Speed signs are a subcategory of regulatory signs.

questions.question: Which sign prohibits vehicles with trailers from entering?
questions.explanation: NO VEHICLES WITH TRAILER is a specific prohibitive/restrictive sign.

questions.question: According to the FDM outline, which regulatory sign subcategory comes first?
questions.explanation: Priority signs are listed first under Regulatory Signs in the outline.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a subcategory of regulatory signs according to the FDM outline?
questions.explanation: Guide signs are a separate major category, not a subcategory of regulatory signs.

questions.question: What is the difference between the STOP sign and the GIVE WAY sign?
options: STOP requires a full stop at the stop line; GIVE WAY requires yielding to vehicles on the right
STOP requires yielding to the right; GIVE WAY requires a full stop
Both require a full stop at all times
questions.explanation: STOP requires a full stop at the designated STOP LINE, while GIVE WAY requires yielding to vehicles on the right side.

questions.question: Which sign indicates that parking and loading are permitted at specific times?
questions.explanation: Allowable parking and loading zone signs permit parking and loading at a given time and place.

questions.question: What does the LEFT TURNER MUST GIVE WAY sign require?
options: Left-turning vehicles have the right of way
Left-turning vehicles must yield to oncoming traffic
questions.explanation: LEFT TURNER MUST GIVE WAY requires left-turning vehicles to give way to other traffic.

questions.question: Which sign prohibits jeepneys from entering a road?
questions.explanation: NO JEEPNEYS is a specific prohibitive/restrictive sign.

questions.question: Which sign prohibits buses from entering a road?
questions.explanation: NO BUSES is a specific prohibitive/restrictive sign.

questions.question: Which sign prohibits cars from entering a road?
questions.explanation: NO CARS is a specific prohibitive/restrictive sign.

questions.question: Which sign prohibits trucks from entering a road?
questions.explanation: NO TRUCKS is a specific prohibitive/restrictive sign.

questions.question: Which sign prohibits motorcycles from entering a road?
questions.explanation: NO MOTORCYCLES is a specific prohibitive/restrictive sign.

questions.question: What is the purpose of warning signs?
options: To inform road users of traffic laws that constitute an offense if disregarded
To warn motorists of potentially hazardous conditions on or adjacent to the road
questions.explanation: Warning signs warn motorists of potentially hazardous conditions on or adjacent to the road.

questions.question: What do warning signs advise motorists to do in the interest of safety?
options: Increase speed to pass through quickly
Call for a reduction in speed
questions.explanation: Warning signs may call for a reduction in speed in the interest of safety.

questions.question: What does a SHARP TURN sign warn about?
options: A gentle bend in the road
questions.explanation: The SHARP TURN sign is a horizontal warning sign indicating a sharp turn ahead.

questions.question: What does the HAIRPIN BEND sign indicate?
options: A gentle curve to the left
A very sharp bend resembling a hairpin
questions.explanation: The HAIRPIN BEND sign warns of an extremely sharp curve.

questions.question: What does the WINDING ROAD sign warn about?
options: A series of curves or winding road ahead
questions.explanation: The WINDING ROAD sign warns of a road with a series of curves ahead.

questions.question: What category of warning signs indicates the type of road curve ahead?
questions.explanation: Horizontal signs are used to indicate the type of road curve ahead of the motorist.

questions.question: What does a T-Junction warning sign indicate?
questions.explanation: The T-Junction sign warns of a T-shaped intersection ahead.

questions.question: What does a Y-Junction warning sign indicate?
questions.explanation: The Y-Junction sign warns of a Y-shaped intersection ahead.

questions.question: What is a roundabout also called in the FDM?
questions.explanation: The FDM refers to a roundabout as a 'Rotunda'.

questions.question: Where are intersection signs installed?
options: In the middle of the intersection
questions.explanation: Intersection signs are installed before an intersection or junction.

questions.question: What is the no-parking zone around a Traffic Lights Ahead sign?
questions.explanation: Driver must not park or stop within six (6) meters of this sign as it reduces visibility.

questions.question: What does the Traffic Lights Ahead sign warn about?
questions.explanation: The Traffic Lights Ahead sign indicates a signalized intersection ahead.

questions.question: What do Advance Warning/Traffic Control Device signs indicate?
options: The presence of STOP and GIVE WAY signs ahead
The presence of a hospital ahead
The presence of an expressway exit
questions.explanation: These signs warn of the presence of STOP and GIVE WAY signs ahead.

questions.question: What does the Stop Sign Ahead warning sign indicate?
options: A STOP sign is located ahead
questions.explanation: The Stop Sign Ahead sign warns motorists that a STOP sign is located ahead.

questions.question: What does the Give Way Sign Ahead warning sign indicate?
options: A GIVE WAY sign is located ahead
questions.explanation: The Give Way Sign Ahead sign warns motorists that a GIVE WAY sign is located ahead.

questions.question: What does the Road Narrows Ahead sign warn about?
questions.explanation: The Road Narrows Ahead sign warns that the road width reduces ahead.

questions.question: What does the Narrow Bridge Ahead sign warn about?
options: A narrow bridge ahead on the road
questions.explanation: The Narrow Bridge Ahead sign warns that a narrow bridge is ahead.

questions.question: What does the Divided Road Ahead sign indicate?
options: Traffic must merge into one lane
questions.explanation: The Divided Road Ahead sign warns that the road ahead splits into a divided highway.

questions.question: What does the End of Divided Road Ahead sign indicate?
options: A divided road is starting ahead
The divided road section is ending ahead
questions.explanation: The End of Divided Road Ahead sign warns that the divided road section is ending.

questions.question: What does the Uneven Road Ahead sign warn about?
questions.explanation: The Uneven Road Ahead sign warns of an uneven road surface ahead.

questions.question: What does the Hump Ahead sign warn about?
options: A hump or bump on the road ahead
questions.explanation: The Hump Ahead sign warns of a hump or raised portion on the road ahead.

questions.question: What does the Downhill sign warn about?
questions.explanation: The Downhill sign warns motorists of a downhill slope ahead.

questions.question: What does the Uphill sign warn about?
questions.explanation: The Uphill sign warns motorists of an uphill slope ahead.

questions.question: What does the Slippery Road sign warn about?
questions.explanation: The Slippery Road sign warns of a road surface that may be slippery.

questions.question: What does the Flood-Prone Area sign warn about?
options: An area prone to flooding ahead
questions.explanation: The Flood-Prone Area sign warns of an area prone to flooding ahead.

questions.question: What does the Landslide-Prone Area sign warn about?
options: An area prone to landslides ahead
questions.explanation: The Landslide-Prone Area sign warns of an area prone to landslides ahead.

questions.question: What does the Animal Crossing Ahead sign warn about?
options: Animals may be crossing the road ahead
questions.explanation: The Animal Crossing Ahead sign warns that animals may be crossing the road ahead.

questions.question: What does the Low-Flying Airplane Zone sign warn about?
questions.explanation: The Low-Flying Airplane Zone sign warns that low-flying aircraft may be present.

questions.question: What does the Opening Bridge Ahead sign warn about?
options: A drawbridge or bridge that can open ahead
questions.explanation: The Opening Bridge Ahead sign warns of a bridge that can open ahead.

questions.question: What does the Pedestrian Crossing Ahead sign warn about?
questions.explanation: The Pedestrian Crossing Ahead sign warns of a pedestrian crossing ahead.

questions.question: What does the Children Crossing Ahead sign require?
options: Be aware of and stop for children crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Motorists must be aware of and stop for children crossing ahead.

questions.question: What does the PWDs Crossing Ahead sign warn about?
questions.explanation: The sign warns of Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) crossing ahead.

questions.question: What does the pedestrian crossing at designated areas sign advise?
options: Advising pedestrians to cross at designated areas
Vehicles must cross at designated areas
questions.explanation: The sign advises pedestrians to cross at designated areas.

questions.question: What does the bicycle lane ahead warning sign tell motorists?
options: Be aware and slowdown on bicycle lane ahead
Motorcycles must use the bicycle lane
Bicycles must move to the sidewalk
questions.explanation: Motorists should be aware and slow down on the bicycle lane ahead.

questions.question: What must vehicles do at a railroad crossing?
options: Stop at the designated stop line or drive with caution
Turn around and find another route
questions.explanation: Vehicles must stop at the designated stop line or drive with caution.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an alternative railway crossing sign?
options: It indicates the railway crossing is closed
It is positioned in an area that can be easily seen
It warns of a faster train route
It indicates a pedestrian railway crossing
questions.explanation: The alternative railway crossing sign is positioned in an area that can be easily seen.

questions.question: What does the WHEN WET supplementary sign indicate?
options: It stands alone as a warning
It is combined with the Slippery Road warning sign
It warns of wet paint on the road
questions.explanation: WHEN WET is combined with the Slippery Road warning sign.

questions.question: What do supplementary warning signs for PWDs, Senior Citizens, Schools and Playground indicate?
options: These groups are prohibited from crossing
They warn of the presence of these groups
Vehicles must stop for all pedestrians
questions.explanation: Supplementary signs warn motorists of PWDs, Senior Citizens, Schools and Playground.

questions.question: What does the vertical clearance sign with 5.20 meters indicate?
options: Vehicles must be at least 5.20 meters high
Maximum height of a vehicle must be 5.20 meters or less
questions.explanation: The vertical clearance sign indicates maximum vehicle height of 5.20 meters or less.

questions.question: What does the vertical clearance sign with 4.80 meters indicate?
options: Vehicles must be at least 4.80 meters high
Maximum height of a vehicle must be 4.80 meters or less
The clearance is only for trucks
questions.explanation: The vertical clearance sign indicates maximum vehicle height of 4.80 meters or less.

questions.question: What does the supplementary sign for roadworks ahead indicate?
questions.explanation: The supplementary sign provides additional information about roadworks ahead.

questions.question: What does the supplementary sign for PUJ/buses indicate?
options: The sign applies to PUJ and bus lanes or routes
PUJs and buses must sound their horns
PUJs and buses must speed up
questions.explanation: The supplementary sign indicates applicability to PUJ and buses.

questions.question: What does the Distance to next hazard area supplementary sign show?
options: The distance to the nearest town
The distance to the next hazard area
The distance to the nearest gas station
The remaining length of the road
questions.explanation: This supplementary sign indicates the distance to the next hazard area.

questions.question: What does the DOUBLE SHARP TURN sign warn about?
options: One sharp turn followed by a straight road
Two sharp turns in close succession
A winding road with many curves
questions.explanation: The DOUBLE SHARP TURN sign warns of two sharp turns in close succession.

questions.question: What does the DOUBLE CURVE sign warn about?
options: One sharp curve followed by a straight road
questions.explanation: The DOUBLE CURVE sign warns of two curves in close succession.

questions.question: What does the Approach to Intersection Merging Traffic sign indicate?
options: An intersection with a stop sign
An intersection where merging traffic will enter

questions.question: What does the Spill Way sign warn about?

questions.question: What does the DOUBLE SHARP TURN sign warn about?

questions.question: What is the preferred maximum speed supplementary sign used for?
options: Indicating preferred maximum speed during normal weather traffic conditions
Setting speed limits only for trucks

questions.question: What does the railway crossing warning sign indicate?
options: A warning that a railway crossing is ahead
questions.explanation: The railway crossing warning sign warns of a railway crossing ahead.

questions.question: What do Advance Direction Signs provide?

questions.question: How far before an intersection are Intersection Direction Signs visible?

questions.explanation: Intersection Direction Signs are visible in less than 1 kilometer before an intersection.

questions.question: What do Reassurance Direction Signs indicate?

The approximate distance of a particular exit
The speed limit on the road

questions.question: What do Fingerboard Direction Signs provide?

questions.question: What do Street Name Signs provide?
options: The names of roads and streets that road users are passing or entering
questions.explanation: Street Name Signs provide the names of roads and streets.

questions.question: What do Town Names and Geographical Feature signs convey?
options: General information such as geographical locations, boundaries, and features
The speed limit within the town

questions.question: Which of these is a service sign according to the FDM?

questions.question: Which service sign indicates the location of a gasoline station?

questions.question: Which service sign indicates accommodation for travelers?
questions.explanation: The Accommodation Hotel/Motel sign is a service sign.

questions.question: Which service sign indicates the location of an airport?
questions.explanation: The Airport sign is listed among the service signs.

questions.question: What do Route Markers identify?
options: The speed limit on the highway
The identification route number of arterial and national highways and direction
The name of the nearest town
The distance to the next exit

From the national highway mile marker

To indicate speed limits on Asian highways

questions.question: What type of sign is a Hospital sign?

questions.question: Which sign indicates the location of a rest area or picnic ground?

questions.question: Which service sign indicates truck parking?

questions.question: What do Tourist Information and Tourist Destination signs provide?

questions.question: What is the Asian Highway Leg Marker Sign used for?

Marking segments or legs of the Asian Highway route
Marking exit points on Asian highways

questions.question: What are advance directional signs with route marker shields?

Signs that combine directional information with the route marker shield

questions.question: Which guide sign subcategory provides names of roads and streets being passed?

questions.question: Which service sign indicates a place to eat?

questions.question: Which service sign indicates rest rooms?
questions.explanation: The Rest Rooms sign is listed among service signs.

questions.question: Which service sign indicates first aid services?

To be installed in advance or at the nearest intersection or interchange leading to the expressway

To provide advanced information so drivers can position their vehicles in the correct lanes
To set speed limits on the expressway
To mark parking areas on the expressway

questions.question: What does the LANE DIRECTION sign on an expressway indicate?
options: The speed limit for each lane
Used to guide the motorists into correct lanes leading to an interchange

questions.question: What does the PROHIBITED ON EXPRESSWAY sign indicate?

questions.question: What do TOLL CHARGES signs on expressways inform motorists about?
options: The speed limit at the toll plaza
The amount of toll charges required to pay at the toll plaza
The distance to the next exit
The operating hours of the toll plaza
questions.explanation: TOLL CHARGES signs inform motorists of the amount of toll charges required at the toll plaza.

questions.question: Where are Advance Exit Signs placed on an expressway?
options: Placed in advance of an exit toll

questions.question: Where are Expressway Exit Direction Signs posted?
options: Posted overhead before the exit ramp of the interchange
In the middle of the expressway
questions.explanation: Expressway Exit Direction Signs are posted overhead before the exit ramp of the interchange.

questions.question: What do Expressway Service Signs indicate?
options: Distance and direction to rest areas and various expressway services
questions.explanation: Expressway Service Signs show distance and direction to rest areas and various expressway services.

questions.question: What do Start and End of Expressway Signs indicate?
options: The beginning and termination of the expressway
questions.explanation: Start and End of Expressway Signs mark where the expressway begins and ends.

questions.question: At what distance from the toll exit can special expressway signs be seen?
questions.explanation: Special signs on expressways can be seen 200 meters from the toll exit.

questions.question: What are Expressway Traffic Instruction and Regulatory Signs?
options: Signs used on all types of roads
Special signs normally seen exclusively for expressways
Signs for pedestrian crossings on expressways
questions.explanation: These are special signs normally seen exclusively for expressways.

questions.question: Which expressway sign guides motorists into correct lanes at an interchange?
options: LANE DIRECTION signs under Expressway Information Signs
questions.explanation: LANE DIRECTION signs guide motorists into correct lanes leading to an interchange.

questions.question: What do Expressway Service Signs for rest areas show?
options: Only the name of the rest area
Distance and direction to rest areas
The services available at the rest area
The operating hours of the rest area
questions.explanation: Expressway Service Signs show the distance and direction to rest areas.

questions.question: How many subcategories of expressway signs are listed in the FDM outline?
questions.explanation: Seven subcategories: Approach, Information, Advance Exit, Exit Direction, Service, Start/End, and Traffic Instruction/Regulatory.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Traffic Instruction Signs?
options: To instruct motorists to follow a direction or obey a course of action
questions.explanation: Traffic Instruction Signs instruct motorists to follow a direction or obey a course of action.

questions.question: How do Traffic Instruction Signs relate to other signs?
options: They work independently of other signs
They are used in conjunction with regulatory or warning signs to support traffic rules
They are only used on expressways
questions.explanation: Traffic Instruction Signs are used in conjunction with regulatory or warning signs to support the operation of traffic rules.

questions.question: What does the Driver must slow down movement instruction sign mean?
questions.explanation: The sign instructs the driver to slow down.

questions.question: What does the Stop on designated stop line sign mean?
options: Stop exactly at the designated stop line
Stop only if there is traffic
questions.explanation: The sign instructs the driver to stop on the designated stop line.

questions.question: What does the sign Vehicle may turn left or right if the intersection is clear mean?
options: Vehicles may turn left or right only when the intersection is clear
Vehicles may turn regardless of traffic
questions.explanation: Vehicles may turn left or right provided the intersection is clear of traffic.

questions.question: What height restriction triggers the detour requirement for vehicles?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with more than 4.8 meters in height must detour.

questions.question: What does the Driver must give way to pedestrians sign mean?
options: Pedestrians must give way to vehicles
The driver must yield the right of way to pedestrians
Only pedestrians at crosswalks must give way
Vehicles and pedestrians share equal priority
questions.explanation: The sign instructs the driver to give way to pedestrians.

questions.question: What does the Turn right on green light only sign mean?
options: Right turns are allowed at any time
Right turns are permitted only when the traffic light is green
Right turns are allowed on red
questions.explanation: The sign instructs drivers to turn right only when the traffic light is green.

questions.question: What does the Stay on right lane unless passing other vehicles sign mean?
options: Vehicles should always stay in the left lane
Vehicles should stay on the right lane and only use the left lane for passing
Vehicles should drive in the middle of the road
Passing is prohibited at all times
questions.explanation: Stay on the right lane unless passing other vehicles.

questions.question: What does the Approaching Dead End sign indicate?
options: The road ahead has no exit
questions.explanation: The Approaching Dead End sign warns that the road ahead comes to an end.

questions.question: What does the Road is closed to all vehicles sign mean?
options: No vehicles are allowed to use the road
Only local residents may use the road
The road is open only at night
questions.explanation: The road is closed to all vehicles.

questions.question: What does the Drivers to form one lane only sign mean?
options: Vehicles should spread across all lanes
Vehicles must merge and form a single lane
Only one vehicle is allowed on the road
questions.explanation: Drivers must merge and form only one lane of traffic.

questions.question: What are Detour Directional Signs used for?
options: To mark the main route ahead
To provide alternative routing directions when the main route is closed
questions.explanation: Detour Directional Signs provide alternative route directions when the main road is not passable.

questions.question: What are Directional Signs for Trucks and Buses?
options: Signs that provide specific directions for trucks and buses
Signs that set speed limits for trucks and buses
Signs that mark parking areas for trucks and buses
questions.explanation: Directional signs for trucks and buses provide specific routing directions for these vehicles.

questions.question: What are the two types of Traffic Instruction Signs?
options: Supplementary signs and Movement Instruction signs
questions.explanation: Traffic Instruction Signs are divided into Supplementary Signs and Movement Instruction Signs.

questions.question: What distinguishes supplementary signs from movement instruction signs?
options: Supplementary signs provide additional text information; movement instruction signs give direct commands
Supplementary signs are only for pedestrians; movement instruction signs are only for vehicles
Supplementary signs are placed above movement instruction signs
questions.explanation: Supplementary signs provide additional qualifying information, while movement instruction signs give specific directives.

questions.question: What is the purpose of hazard markers?
options: To mark safe zones on the road
To emphasize a marked change in the direction of travel and the presence of an obstruction
questions.explanation: Hazard markers emphasize a marked change in the direction of travel and the presence of an obstruction.

questions.question: What do One-Way Hazard Markers indicate?
options: The only direction allowed at the end of the road
questions.explanation: One-Way Hazard Markers indicate the only direction allowed at the end of the road.

questions.question: What do Two-Way Hazard Markers indicate?
options: The road ahead is about to change direction
questions.explanation: Two-Way Hazard Markers warn that the road ahead is about to change direction.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Chevron signs?
options: To guide drivers through a change in horizontal alignment of the road
questions.explanation: Chevron signs guide drivers through a change in horizontal alignment of the road.

questions.question: What do Width Markers indicate?
questions.explanation: Width Markers indicate narrowing width clearance on the road.

questions.question: What do Obstruction Markers indicate?
questions.explanation: Obstruction Markers indicate road closure ahead.

questions.question: Where is a hazard marker sign placed on an overpass or median island?
options: On the ground next to the structure
On a wide column of an overpass structure or median island
Above the road on a gantry
questions.explanation: A hazard marker is used on a wide column of an overpass structure or median island.

questions.question: What are the two main types of hazard markers listed in the FDM outline?
options: One-Way Hazard and Two-Way Hazard markers
questions.explanation: The FDM outline lists One-Way Hazard and Two-Way Hazard as the two main types of hazard markers.

questions.question: What is the difference between one-way and two-way hazard markers?
options: One-way shows allowed direction; two-way warns of direction change ahead
One-way warns of direction change; two-way shows allowed direction
One-way is for expressways; two-way is for regular roads
questions.explanation: One-Way markers indicate the only direction allowed at the road's end; Two-Way markers warn of a direction change ahead.

questions.question: What does a PREFERRED MAXIMUM SPEED sign indicate during normal weather traffic conditions?
options: The legal maximum speed for the road
The recommended maximum speed during normal weather traffic conditions
The minimum speed on the road
The speed limit during rain only
questions.explanation: The supplementary sign 'Preferred maximum speed during normal weather traffic conditions' indicates the recommended maximum speed under normal weather conditions.

questions.question: Where in the FDM outline do roadwork signs appear?
options: As a separate category G after hazard markers
questions.explanation: Roadwork Signs are category G in the outline, appearing after Hazard Markers (F).

questions.question: Which supplementary warning sign is used for roadworks?
questions.explanation: An additional sign on roadworks ahead is used as a supplementary sign with roadwork warnings.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a main road traffic sign category in the FDM outline?
questions.explanation: The FDM outline lists A-Regulatory, B-Warning, C-Guide, D-Expressway, E-Traffic Instruction, F-Hazard Markers, G-Roadwork. Expressway Exit Markers is not a top-level category.

questions.question: What should a driver do when approaching a roadwork sign?
options: Speed up to pass the area quickly
Reduce speed and proceed with caution
Ignore the sign and maintain speed
questions.explanation: Like all warning signs, roadwork signs indicate conditions requiring caution and a reduction in speed.

questions.question: What are pavement markings according to the FDM?
options: Only road signs painted on walls
Lines, symbols, messages, or numerals set into, applied upon, or attached to the pavement
Only center lines on the road
Decorative patterns on the road surface
questions.explanation: Pavement markings are lines, symbols, messages, or numerals set into, applied upon, or attached to the pavement.

questions.question: What do pavement markings supplement?
options: Traffic signals and road signs, serving as other traffic control devices
questions.explanation: Pavement markings are used as a supplement to other traffic control devices such as traffic signals and road signs.

questions.question: What does a solid white center line indicate?
options: Crossing of solid white lines requires special care and is discouraged
questions.explanation: Crossing of solid white lines requires special care and is discouraged.

questions.question: What does a lane line allow a driver to do?
options: Change lanes only with a police escort
Change lanes, provided it is safe and will not result in obstruction
questions.explanation: Changing of lane is allowed provided that it is safe and will not result in obstruction.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines mean?
options: Overtaking is allowed but crossing is not
Overtaking and crossing are both allowed
Crossing is allowed but overtaking is not
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no overtaking and no crossing.

questions.question: What does a single solid yellow line mean?
options: Crossing is allowed but no overtaking
Overtaking is allowed but no crossing
Both overtaking and crossing are allowed
questions.explanation: A single solid yellow line means crossing is allowed but no overtaking.

questions.question: What does a single yellow line with a broken white line mean?
options: No overtaking but crossing allowed on solid yellow side; overtaking and crossing allowed on broken white side
Crossing is prohibited on both sides
questions.explanation: Solid yellow side: no overtaking, crossing allowed. Broken white side: overtaking and crossing allowed.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line mean?
options: Overtaking is allowed but crossing is not
Crossing and overtaking is allowed with necessary precaution
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means crossing and overtaking is allowed with necessary precaution.

questions.question: What does a broken and solid yellow line combination mean?
options: Crossing and overtaking allowed on both sides
Crossing and overtaking allowed on broken side with caution; overtaking not allowed on solid side
Only trucks may cross the solid line
questions.explanation: Overtaking is allowed on the broken side with caution but not on the solid side.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an edge line?
options: To mark the center of the road
To separate the outside edge of the road from the shoulder
questions.explanation: An edge line separates the outside edge of the road from the shoulder.

questions.question: What does a continuity line on the left side indicate?
options: The lane is ending or exiting and the driver must change lanes to continue
questions.explanation: A continuity line on the left means the lane is ending or exiting; driver must change lanes to continue.

questions.question: What does a continuity line on the right side mean?
questions.explanation: Continuity lines on the right means that the lane will continue unaffected.

questions.question: What do transition lines guide traffic past?
options: Obstructions such as islands, median strips, and bridge piers
questions.explanation: Transition lines guide traffic safely to pass obstructions such as islands, median strips, and bridge piers.

questions.question: What is a stop line?
options: A line that indicates the speed limit
A white line before which vehicles are required to stop
A line that marks the edge of the road
A line that separates traffic lanes
questions.explanation: A stop line is a white line that vehicles are required to stop before crossing.

questions.question: What do Give Way or Holding Lines consist of?
options: Two broken white lines across the carriageway
questions.explanation: Give Way or Holding Lines consist of two broken white lines across the carriageway.

questions.question: At give way or holding lines, what must drivers do?
options: Give way to all traffic in accordance with the standard sign
questions.explanation: Drivers must give way to all traffic in accordance with the standard sign.

questions.question: At a roundabout, who has the right-of-way?
options: Vehicles about to enter the roundabout
Vehicles within the rotunda have the right-of-way over vehicles entering
The larger vehicle always has priority
questions.explanation: Vehicles within the rotunda have the right-of-way over vehicles which are just about to enter.

questions.question: What is a turn line used for?
options: To mark the center of the road
To guide vehicles through a turning movement at intersections
questions.explanation: Turn lines guide vehicles through a turning movement at intersections.

questions.question: What is a parking bay marking used for?
options: To designate parking space, with note of PWD Parking Mark
questions.explanation: Parking bay markings designate parking space and include a note about PWD Parking Mark.

questions.question: What is a loading and unloading bay lane line?
options: A broken yellow line for buses
A solid white line indicating the proper location with parking restrictions
A double yellow line for trucks
A red line for emergency vehicles
questions.explanation: The loading and unloading bay lane line is a solid white line indicating the proper location with parking restrictions.

questions.question: What does the yellow box marking at an intersection indicate?
options: Parking is allowed inside the box
No vehicle should stay inside the box to avoid obstruction to other motorists
Only buses may stay inside the box
Vehicles may stop inside the box for 30 seconds
questions.explanation: The yellow box with diagonal lines forming an X means no vehicle should stay inside to avoid obstruction.

questions.question: What does the yellow box consist of?
options: Yellow lines on the side of the road
A yellow box within the intersection and yellow diagonal lines forming an X inside the box
questions.explanation: The yellow box has lines forming a box within the intersection and yellow diagonal lines forming an X.

questions.question: What is the bus and PUJ lane line?
options: A broken white line for buses only
A solid yellow line used to separate other vehicles from buses and PUJs
A double white line for public transport
questions.explanation: The bus and PUJ lane line is a solid yellow line separating other vehicles from buses and PUJs, supplemented by raised pavement markers.

questions.question: What are traffic cones and concrete barriers classified as?
questions.explanation: Traffic cones on the road and concrete barriers are classified under Object Markings.

questions.question: What is a Cat's Eye in pavement markings?
options: A raised pavement marker that serves as a substitute to lane lines
A warning sign for animal crossings
questions.explanation: Cat's Eye is a raised pavement marker that serves as a substitute to lane lines.

questions.question: What are chevron pavement markings used for?
options: To guide traffic into the right turning lanes separated by an island at a signalized intersection
questions.explanation: Chevron pavement markings guide traffic into right turning lanes separated by an island at a signalized intersection.

questions.question: What do rumble strips provide to motorists?
options: Visual, audio, and motion warnings on the road
questions.explanation: Rumble strips provide motorists with visual, audio, and motion warnings on the road.

questions.question: What do rumble strips produce when a vehicle runs over them?
options: A humming sound and ample bumpy ride
questions.explanation: Rumble strips produce a humming sound and ample bumpy ride to the motorists when run over.

questions.question: What do painted curbs indicate?
options: The speed limit on the road
No loading and unloading, or no parking zones
questions.explanation: Painted curbs indicate No Loading and Unloading zones or No Parking zones.

questions.question: What does the railroad crossing ahead pavement marking indicate?
options: A railroad crossing is ahead on the road
questions.explanation: The railroad crossing ahead pavement marking warns of a railroad crossing ahead.

questions.question: What are motorcycle lanes?
options: Lanes exclusive to motorcycles with no sharing
Lanes allotted for motorcycle riders that can be shared with other vehicles
questions.explanation: Motorcycle lanes are allotted for motorcycle riders and can be shared with other vehicles.

questions.question: When must a motorcycle rider signal intention when turning into an intersection?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders turning into an intersection must signal their intention within 100 meters.

questions.question: Can motorcycle riders stay on lanes other than motorcycle lanes?
options: Only when instructed by enforcers or turning into an intersection
questions.explanation: Riders are not allowed to stay on other lanes unless instructed by enforcers or turning into an intersection.

questions.question: What are bus lanes used for?
options: Designated lanes for buses only; bus drivers are not allowed to use other lanes
questions.explanation: Bus lanes are designated for buses; bus drivers are not allowed to use other lanes except when turning or instructed.

questions.question: When may bus drivers use lanes other than bus lanes?
options: When instructed by enforcers or when turning into an intersection
questions.explanation: Bus drivers may use other lanes when instructed by enforcers or when turning into an intersection.

questions.question: How is a bicycle lane marked on the pavement?
options: By a broken white line in the center of the road
By a solid line along either side of the road
By a yellow box with an X
questions.explanation: A bicycle lane is painted on the pavement by a solid line along either side of the road.

questions.question: Are motor vehicles allowed to use bicycle lanes?
options: Yes, if there is no bicycle present
Motor vehicles are not allowed to use this lane
Only motorcycles may use bicycle lanes
questions.explanation: Motor vehicles are not allowed to use the bicycle lane.

questions.question: What color are pavement arrows?
questions.explanation: Pavement arrows are used for lane control and in white color.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a speed limit painted on the pavement?
options: To replace all roadside speed limit signs
To supplement the speed limit posted on the roadside
To indicate the minimum speed only
To mark the end of a speed zone
questions.explanation: A speed limit on pavement supplements the speed limit posted on the roadside.

questions.question: What speed limit example is given for pavement speed markings?
questions.explanation: The FDM shows a speed limit at 60 KPH as the example of a pavement speed marking.

questions.question: What do approach markings to islands and obstructions indicate?
options: How to navigate around islands and obstructions on the road
The distance to the next island
questions.explanation: Approach markings to islands and obstructions guide vehicles safely around these features.

questions.question: What are rumble strips made of?
questions.explanation: Rumble strips are thermoplastic lane markings designed to provide warnings on the road.

questions.question: What do pavement markings do besides guiding traffic?
options: Give advance warning and may impose restrictions supported by traffic regulations
questions.explanation: Pavement markings guide traffic, give advance warning, or may impose restrictions supported by traffic regulations.

questions.question: What are the two types of pedestrian intersection markings based on traffic control?
questions.explanation: The FDM lists pedestrian intersections as signalized (with traffic signals) and non-signalized (without signals).

questions.question: What do transition lines also indicate besides guiding past obstructions?
options: Changes in the width of the traveled portion and an increase or reduction in traffic lanes
questions.explanation: Transition lines indicate changes in width of the traveled portion and increase or reduction in traffic lanes.

questions.question: What is the function of regulatory signs as a whole?
options: To provide directions to tourist spots
To inform road users of traffic laws and regulations which, if disregarded, will constitute an offense
To warn of hazardous road conditions
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs inform road users of traffic laws and regulations which, if disregarded, will constitute an offense.

questions.question: What is the penalty for disregarding a regulatory sign?
questions.explanation: The FDM states that regulatory signs, if disregarded, will constitute an offense.

questions.question: Which signs are installed before an intersection or junction?
questions.explanation: Intersection signs are installed before an intersection or junction.

questions.question: What does the Side Road Junction Ahead sign indicate?
options: A side road joins the main road ahead
questions.explanation: The Side Road Junction Ahead sign warns that a side road joins the main road ahead.

questions.question: What does the Intersection Ahead sign warn about?
options: An intersection is ahead on the road
questions.explanation: The Intersection Ahead sign warns of an intersection ahead on the road.

questions.question: What warning sign indicates approach to an intersection with a side road?
questions.explanation: Approach to intersection side road warns of an intersection with a side road.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a horizontal warning sign?
questions.explanation: T-Junction is an Intersection sign, not a Horizontal sign. Horizontal signs include curve-related warnings.

questions.question: Why must drivers not park within 6 meters of a Traffic Lights Ahead sign?
options: Because it is illegal on all roads
Because it reduces visibility for other drivers
Because it is only for emergency vehicles
Because it blocks the pedestrian path
questions.explanation: Parking within 6 meters reduces visibility for other drivers.

questions.question: Which guide sign provides reassurance about the route by showing exit distance?
questions.explanation: Reassurance Direction Signs provide approximate distance of a particular exit.

questions.question: What do Philippine Highway Network route markers use as a reference point in each province?
options: Zero Kilometer Post near the Provincial Building
questions.explanation: Distance is measured from Zero Kilometer Post in each Province near the Provincial Building.

questions.question: Which service signs are listed together under accommodation?
questions.explanation: The Accommodation service sign lists Hotel and Motel together.

questions.question: Which service sign indicates a place for picnics?
questions.explanation: The Rest Area, Picnic Ground sign is listed among service signs.

questions.question: Which service sign indicates facilities for persons with disabilities?
questions.explanation: The Disabled Service sign is listed among the service signs.

questions.question: Which service sign indicates a litter bin?
questions.explanation: The Litter Bin sign is listed among the service signs.

questions.question: Which service sign indicates an ambulance service?
questions.explanation: The Ambulance sign is listed among the service signs.

questions.question: Which service sign indicates a campground for caravans?
questions.explanation: The Caravan Camping Site sign is listed among the service signs.

questions.question: Which service sign indicates an information center?
questions.explanation: The Information Center sign is listed among the service signs.

questions.question: Which service sign indicates a telephone?
questions.explanation: The Telephone sign is listed among the service signs.

questions.question: What is the sequence of expressway sign subcategories as listed in the FDM?
options: Exit, Approach, Information, Service, Start/End, Traffic Instruction
Approach, Information, Advance Exit, Exit Direction, Service, Start/End, Traffic Instruction
Traffic Instruction, Approach, Information, Exit, Service, Start/End
Start/End, Approach, Information, Exit, Service, Traffic Instruction
questions.explanation: The FDM lists them in order: Approach, Information, Advance Exit, Exit Direction, Service, Start/End, Traffic Instruction and Regulatory.

questions.question: What information does an Expressway Approach Sign provide?
options: Direction to the expressway entrance at the nearest intersection or interchange
Rest area locations on the expressway
questions.explanation: Expressway Approach Signs are installed in advance of or at the nearest intersection or interchange leading to the expressway.

questions.question: What does a detour directional sign indicate?
options: The main road is clear ahead
An alternative route must be taken due to a road closure or obstruction
The road is a one-way street
questions.explanation: Detour directional signs provide directions for alternative routes when the main route is impassable.

questions.question: What does the traffic instruction sign about vehicles with more than 4.8 meters height require?
options: They must turn on hazard lights
They must get an escort vehicle
questions.explanation: Vehicles with more than 4.8 meters in height must detour.

questions.question: What is the function of a sign used on a wide column of an overpass structure?
options: To indicate the height of the overpass
To serve as a hazard marker on the structure
To show direction to the nearest exit
questions.explanation: A sign used on a wide column of an overpass structure or median island serves as a hazard marker.

questions.question: How do chevron hazard marker signs differ from chevron pavement markings?
options: Chevron signs are vertical above-ground guides; pavement chevrons are painted on the road
Chevron signs are for highways only
Chevron markings are for parking lots only
questions.explanation: Chevron signs guide drivers through horizontal alignment changes; chevron pavement markings guide into turning lanes at intersections.

questions.question: What happens when a continuity line is on the left side of a lane?
options: The road is about to widen
The lane is ending or exiting; the driver must change lanes to continue in the current direction
The road is merging with another road
questions.explanation: Continuity line on the left side means the lane is ending or exiting and the driver must change lanes.

questions.question: What supplement do bus and PUJ lane lines receive?
questions.explanation: Bus and PUJ lane lines are supplemented by raised pavement markers.

questions.question: What does the yield or holding line require drivers to do?
options: Give way to all traffic in accordance with the standard sign
questions.explanation: At holding lines, drivers must give way to all traffic in accordance with the standard sign.

questions.question: What do all pavement markings collectively provide?
options: Guidance, advance warning, and restrictions supported by traffic regulations
questions.explanation: Pavement markings guide traffic, give advance warning, or may impose restrictions supported by traffic regulations.

questions.question: Why does the FDM advise reduction in speed near warning signs?
options: To avoid getting a speeding ticket
In the interest of safety and that of other road users
Because the road is always closed ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs may call for a reduction in speed, in the interest of safety and that of other road users.

questions.question: What is the difference between No Stopping and No Parking signs?
options: No Stopping prohibits any stopping; No Parking allows stopping but not leaving the vehicle
Both signs mean the same thing
No Parking is stricter than No Stopping
No Stopping applies only to trucks
questions.explanation: The FDM lists No Stopping Anytime and No Parking restrictions separately, with No Stopping being the more restrictive prohibition.

questions.question: What type of sign is a No Blowing of Horns sign?
questions.explanation: No Blowing of Horns is listed under Miscellaneous Signs in the regulatory signs category.

questions.question: What is the Republic Act number for the Seat Belt Law?
questions.explanation: The USE SEAT BELT sign is used pursuant to R.A. No. 8750, the Seat Belt Law.

questions.question: What does the yellow box sign prohibit in terms of stopping and parking?
options: Both stopping and parking are prohibited anytime within the yellow box
Parking is allowed for delivery vehicles
questions.explanation: No stopping or parking is allowed anytime within the yellow box.

questions.question: What does the Divided Road Ahead sign warn motorists about?
options: The road splits into separate carriageways ahead
questions.explanation: Divided Road Ahead warns that the road ahead splits into a divided highway.

questions.question: What does the End of Divided Road sign indicate?
options: Traffic must split into two lanes
The divided highway section is ending and traffic may merge
questions.explanation: End of Divided Road Ahead indicates the divided road section is ending.

questions.question: What combination of signs is the WHEN WET sign used with?
questions.explanation: WHEN WET is combined with the Slippery Road warning sign.

questions.question: What does the distance to next hazard supplementary sign help with?
options: Preparing for the upcoming hazard at the indicated distance
questions.explanation: The distance sign helps motorists prepare for the hazard at the indicated distance.

questions.question: Which warning sign category includes flood-prone, landslide-prone, and slippery road?
questions.explanation: Flood-prone area, landslide-prone area, and slippery road are under Road Obstacle Signs.

questions.question: Which two vertical clearance heights are specifically listed in the warning signs?
questions.explanation: The vertical clearance signs list maximum heights of 5.20 meters or less and 4.80 meters or less.

questions.question: What do pedestrian warning signs advise pedestrians?
options: To cross anywhere on the road
questions.explanation: The pedestrian warning sign advises pedestrians to cross at designated areas.

questions.question: What does the PWD crossing warning sign indicate?
options: An area where persons with disabilities may be crossing
questions.explanation: The sign warns of Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) crossing ahead.

questions.question: What does RIGHT TURNER CROSS AT BROKEN LINES allow within a BUS/PUJ zone?
options: Vehicles from any lane may cross to turn right
Vehicles from the left lane may cross the broken line to turn right
Only buses may cross the broken line
No one may cross the broken line
questions.explanation: Vehicles from the left lane may cross the broken line to turn right within the BUS/PUJ zone.

questions.question: What is the specific restriction for the fire hydrant zone according to the FDM?
questions.explanation: The source explicitly states 'No waiting within 4 meters' for the fire hydrant sign.

questions.question: What does the advance directional sign with route marker shield combine?
options: Directional information with the route marker identifier
questions.explanation: Advance directional signs with route marker shields combine directional information with the route marker.

questions.question: What does a Refreshment service sign indicate?
options: A place for drinks and light meals
questions.explanation: The Refreshment service sign indicates a place where refreshments are available.

questions.question: What distinguishes Expressway Traffic Instruction and Regulatory Signs from regular signs?
options: They are special signs normally seen exclusively for expressways
They are placed on the ground only
questions.explanation: These special signs are normally seen exclusively for expressways.

questions.question: What does the expressway service sign for various services show?
options: Distance and direction to various expressway services
questions.explanation: Expressway service signs show both distance and direction to various expressway services.

questions.question: Where are expressway approach signs installed?
options: In advance or at the nearest intersection or interchange leading to the expressway
questions.explanation: Expressway Approach Signs are installed in advance or at the nearest intersection or interchange leading to the expressway.

questions.question: What does an Advance Exit Sign on an expressway prepare a driver for?
options: An upcoming exit from the expressway
questions.explanation: Advance Exit Signs are placed in advance of an exit toll to prepare drivers for an upcoming exit.

questions.question: What do one-way hazard markers specifically indicate to an approaching driver?
options: The road ahead has two directions
The only direction allowed at the end of the road
questions.explanation: One-Way Hazard Markers indicate the only direction allowed at the end of the road.

questions.question: What is the purpose of two-way hazard markers?
options: To warn the driver that the road ahead is about to change direction
questions.explanation: Two-Way Hazard Markers warn that the road ahead is about to change direction.

questions.question: According to the FDM, which are the primary categories of hazard markers?
options: One-way and two-way hazard markers only
One-way and two-way hazard markers, plus chevron, width, and obstruction markers
questions.explanation: The FDM lists One-Way and Two-Way Hazard Markers as the main categories, and also includes Chevron signs, Width Markers, Obstruction Markers, and signs on overpass/median columns.

questions.question: What is the function of traffic instruction signs in conjunction with regulatory signs?
options: To support the operation of traffic rules as part of a standard treatment
questions.explanation: Traffic instruction signs are used in conjunction with regulatory or warning signs to support the operation of traffic rules.

questions.question: What does the Stay on right lane movement instruction sign mean?
options: Always stay in the left lane
Stay on right lane unless passing other vehicles
Drive in whichever lane you prefer
questions.explanation: Stay on right lane unless passing other vehicles.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the movement instruction sign Turn right on green light only?
options: To restrict right turns to when the traffic signal is green
To allow right turns on red
questions.explanation: The sign restricts right turns to only when the green light is illuminated.

questions.question: What is the main function of a center line?
options: To separate opposing traffic flows and indicate crossing restrictions
questions.explanation: The center/separation line separates traffic flows, with crossing restrictions.

questions.question: What does the X formed by yellow diagonal lines inside the yellow box indicate?
options: No vehicle should stay inside the box
Only emergency vehicles may stay inside
questions.explanation: No vehicle should stay inside the box to avoid obstruction to other motorists.

questions.question: What type of line is used for loading and unloading bays?
questions.explanation: The loading and unloading bay lane line is a solid white line with parking restrictions.

questions.question: Where are bicycle lanes painted on the pavement?
options: In the center of the road
By a solid line along either side of the road
questions.explanation: Bicycle lanes are painted by a solid line along either side of the road.

questions.question: What color are pavement arrows used for lane control?
questions.explanation: Pavement arrows are used for lane control and in white color.

questions.question: What is the purpose of pavement arrows?
options: For lane control and direction guidance
questions.explanation: Pavement arrows are used for lane control purposes.

questions.question: What distinguishes thermoplastic rumble strips from regular lane markings?
options: They provide visual, audio, and motion warnings through humming sound and bumpy ride
They are used only at night
questions.explanation: Rumble strips are thermoplastic lane markings providing visual, audio, and motion warnings.

questions.question: What do chevron pavement markings at a signalized intersection guide?
options: Traffic into right turning lanes separated by a corner island
questions.explanation: Chevron markings guide traffic into right turning lanes separated by an island at a signalized intersection.

questions.question: When are motorcycle riders allowed to leave the motorcycle lane?
options: When instructed by enforcers or when turning into an intersection, signaling within 100 meters
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders may leave when instructed by enforcers or turning into an intersection, signaling within 100 meters.

questions.question: Can bus drivers use lanes other than bus lanes?
options: Only when instructed by enforcers or when turning into an intersection
questions.explanation: Bus drivers are not allowed to use other lanes except when instructed by enforcers or turning into an intersection.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a stop line at an intersection?
options: To indicate where vehicles may park
To mark the point where vehicles are required to stop before the white line
questions.explanation: Vehicles are required to stop before the white stop line at intersections.

questions.question: What does a PWD parking mark indicate in a parking bay?
options: The parking space is designated for persons with disabilities
Only PWD vehicles may pass through
PWDs are not allowed to park
questions.explanation: PWD Parking Mark in a parking bay designates the space for persons with disabilities.

questions.question: How do chevron signs and chevron pavement markings differ in function?
options: Chevron signs are vertical signs for horizontal alignment; pavement chevrons are for turning lane guidance
Chevron signs are for expressways only
Chevron markings are for local roads only
questions.explanation: Chevron signs guide through horizontal alignment changes; pavement chevrons guide into turning lanes at intersections.

questions.question: What type of lane line separates other vehicles from buses and PUJs?
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line is used to separate other vehicles from buses and PUJs.

questions.question: What supplementary sign is used with a warning sign to indicate roadworks ahead?
options: Preferred maximum speed during normal weather traffic conditions
Signs of PWDs, Senior Citizens, Schools and Playground
questions.explanation: The supplementary sign 'Additional sign on roadworks ahead' is used to indicate that roadworks are ahead.

questions.question: What does the 'Additional sign on roadworks ahead' supplementary sign indicate?
questions.explanation: The supplementary sign 'Additional sign on roadworks ahead' indicates that roadwork is ahead.

questions.question: What are the nine subcategories of warning signs in the FDM outline?
options: Horizontal, Vertical, Intersection, Roadwork, Pedestrian, Railway, Supplementary, Animal, Weather
Horizontal, Intersection, Advance Warning/Traffic Control, Road Width, Road Obstacles, Pedestrian, Railway Level Crossing, Supplementary, Other Warning Signs
Curve, Turn, Slope, Bridge, Flood, Landslide, Slippery, Animal, Airplane
Stop, Yield, Merge, Lane, Width, Height, Weight, Speed, Direction
questions.explanation: The nine subcategories are: Horizontal, Intersection, Advance Warning, Road Width, Road Obstacles, Pedestrian, Railway Level Crossing, Supplementary, and Other Warning Signs.

questions.question: What is the comprehensive list of all regulatory sign subcategories in the FDM?
options: Priority, Directional, Prohibitive/Restrictive, Speed, Parking and Stopping, and Miscellaneous
Stop, Yield, Turn, Overtake, and Speed
Entry, Exit, Direction, Speed, and Parking
questions.explanation: The six regulatory subcategories are: Priority, Directional, Prohibitive/Restrictive, Speed, Parking and Stopping, and Miscellaneous.

questions.question: How many subcategories of guide/informative signs are listed in the FDM outline?
questions.explanation: Ten subcategories: 1-Advance Direction, 2-Intersection Direction, 3-Reassurance Direction, 4-Fingerboard Direction, 5-Street Name, 6-Town Names, 7-Service Signs, 8-Tourist Information, 9-Route Markers, 10-Asian Highway Route Markers.

questions.question: What is the complete FDM outline for pavement markings starting with longitudinal lines?
options: Only center lines, lane lines, and edge lines
Center Line, Lane Line, Barrier Line (with sub-types), Edge Line, Continuity Line, and Transition Lines
Only yellow lines and white lines
Only center lines and crossing lines
questions.explanation: Longitudinal Lines include: Center Line, Lane Line, Barrier Line (Double Solid Yellow, Single Solid Yellow, Single Yellow with Broken White, Broken Yellow), Edge Line, Continuity Line, and Transition Lines.

questions.question: According to R.A. No. 4136, when two vehicles approach an intersection at approximately the same time, which vehicle has the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: R.A. No. 4136 states that the driver of the vehicle on the left shall yield the right of way to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: A driver travelling at an unlawful speed who approaches an intersection will have what consequence regarding right-of-way?
options: The driver forfeits any right-of-way they might otherwise have
The driver gets priority over all other vehicles
The driver must stop for exactly 10 seconds
questions.explanation: Under R.A. No. 4136, the driver of any vehicle travelling at an unlawful speed shall forfeit any right of way which he/she might otherwise have.

questions.question: When must a driver yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian crossing a highway?
options: Within a business or residential district at a crosswalk
Only when a traffic enforcer is present
questions.explanation: R.A. No. 4136 requires drivers within a business or residential district to yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian crossing within a crosswalk.

questions.question: A pedestrian crossing a highway within a business district at a point other than a crosswalk must do what?
options: Yield the right-of-way to vehicles upon the highway
Signal to vehicles with hand gestures
Wait for a traffic enforcer to assist
Proceed with the same right-of-way as at a crosswalk
questions.explanation: Every pedestrian crossing a highway within a business or residential district at any point other than a crosswalk shall yield the right-of-way to vehicles upon the highway.

questions.question: A vehicle entering a highway from a private road or driveway must yield the right-of-way to which vehicles?
options: Only vehicles approaching from the right
Only vehicles approaching from the left
All vehicles approaching on such highway
questions.explanation: A driver entering a highway from a private road or drive shall yield the right-of-way to all vehicles approaching on such highway.

questions.question: A driver on a highway must yield the right-of-way to which of the following when they are on official business and sounding an audible signal?
options: Police and fire department vehicles and ambulances
questions.explanation: A driver shall yield the right-of-way to police or fire department vehicles and ambulances when operated on official business and sounding an audible signal.

questions.question: A vehicle entering a through highway or a stop intersection shall yield the right-of-way to vehicles in which direction?
options: Only vehicles approaching from the right
Only vehicles approaching from the left
All vehicles approaching from either direction
Only vehicles that sound their horn
questions.explanation: A driver entering a through highway or stop intersection shall yield the right-of-way to all vehicles approaching in either direction.

questions.question: Vehicle B is approaching but has not yet entered an intersection. Vehicle A is inside the intersection turning left with a plainly visible signal. What must Vehicle B do?
options: Proceed before Vehicle A completes the turn
Yield the right-of-way to Vehicle A
Stop and wait for Vehicle A to go straight
questions.explanation: A driver not yet in an intersection shall yield the right-of-way to a vehicle within such intersection or turning left, provided the left-turning driver has given a visible signal.

questions.question: Which groups should a defensive driver give the right-of-way to at pedestrian crossings?
options: PWDs, Senior Citizens, Children, Pregnant Women, and Road Workers
questions.explanation: A defensive driver should give the right-of-way to pedestrians such as PWDs, Senior Citizens, Children, Pregnant Women, and Road Workers.

questions.question: What must a driver do when an emergency vehicle with siren and flashing lights approaches from behind?
options: Slow down to stop and give way
questions.explanation: Upon approach of any emergency vehicle giving audible signal, the driver shall immediately drive to the right-hand edge or curb and stop.

questions.question: At a roundabout or rotunda, who has the right-of-way?
options: The vehicle on the right entering
questions.explanation: If you are about to enter a roundabout or rotunda, yield the right-of-way to vehicles already inside the roundabout.

questions.question: Which doctrine states that a person who has the last opportunity of avoiding a road crash, despite the negligent acts of the other party, is solely responsible?
questions.explanation: The Doctrine of Last Clear Chance states that a person with the last chance of avoiding a crash is considered in law solely responsible.

questions.question: What does a defensive driver yield the right-of-way to on an incline?
options: Ascending vehicles, school service, and vehicles with lesser steering radius
questions.explanation: A defensive driver should yield to ascending vehicles, school service, and vehicles with lesser steering radius.

questions.question: The Give Way sign requires a driver to yield to vehicles on which side of the intersection?
questions.explanation: The Give Way sign means yield to the vehicles on the right side of the intersection.

questions.question: When approaching a crosswalk or pedestrian lane, what must a driver do?
options: Slow down and stop to yield to pedestrians
Proceed as usual if the crosswalk is empty
questions.explanation: When approaching a crosswalk or pedestrian lane, a driver should slow down and stop to yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: What should you do if you are in doubt while approaching an intersection?
options: Yield the right-of-way to avoid a road crash
questions.explanation: If in doubt approaching an intersection, yield the right-of-way to avoid a road crash.

questions.question: At an intersection, if a car on your right enters at the same time you do, what must you do?
options: Give way, the vehicle on the right has priority right-of-way
questions.explanation: At an intersection, give way to the car on your right because the vehicle on the right has the priority right-of-way.

questions.question: Why should a driver always yield to emergency vehicles with blinkers and sirens on?
options: Because they have a priority right-of-way
Because they pay higher registration fees
