questions.explanation: A driver should always yield to emergency vehicles because they have a priority right-of-way.

questions.question: What does the Left Turner Must Give Way sign mean?
options: Vehicles turning left must yield to oncoming traffic
Vehicles turning right must yield to left-turners
questions.explanation: The Left Turner Must Give Way sign indicates vehicles turning left must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Before turning, to whom is a driver required to give way first?
options: Pedestrians and motor vehicles with the first priority right-of-way
questions.explanation: Before turning, give way to pedestrians and motor vehicles with the first priority right-of-way.

questions.question: What should you do if an oncoming vehicle steers into your direction on a two-way road?
options: Drive to the right, reduce speed, and if necessary drive off the road
Honk loudly and maintain your lane
questions.explanation: To prevent collision: read and analyze the road ahead, drive to the right, reduce speed, and if necessary drive off the road.

questions.question: When you see an intersection with a blank inverted triangle traffic sign, what should you do?
options: Slow down and give way to any vehicle in the intersection
Proceed only if you honk first
questions.explanation: The inverted triangle means give way. Slow down and give way to any vehicle in the intersection.

questions.question: On an expressway, an overtaking vehicle in Lane 1 has what right-of-way status?
options: Overtaking vehicles do not have right-of-way
questions.explanation: Lane 1 is for overtaking only within the allowed speed. Overtaking vehicles, however, do not have right-of-way.

questions.question: What should a driver do when an elderly person crosses a pedestrian lane?
options: Honk to make them move faster
Be patient and allow them to cross
questions.explanation: When an elderly person crosses the pedestrian lane, be patient and allow them to cross.

questions.question: What should you do if you see a person in a wheelchair about to cross the street?
options: Speed up to pass before them
Stop and wait for the PWD to cross the street
Honk so they know you are coming
questions.explanation: Stop and wait for the PWD to cross the street.

questions.question: A driver shall not drive to the left side of the centerline in overtaking unless what condition is met?
options: The vehicle ahead is below the speed limit
The left side is clearly visible and free of oncoming traffic for a sufficient distance
The driver sounds the horn first
questions.explanation: The driver shall not overtake unless the left side is clearly visible and free of oncoming traffic for a sufficient distance ahead.

questions.question: Overtaking is prohibited when approaching the crest of a grade where the drivers view is obstructed within what distance?
questions.explanation: Do not overtake when the drivers view is obstructed within a distance of five hundred feet ahead.

questions.question: When is overtaking another vehicle on the right permitted?
options: At any time on any road
On a highway within a business or residential district having two or more lanes for traffic in one direction
Only when the vehicle ahead is a motorcycle
questions.explanation: On a highway within a business or residential district with two or more lanes for traffic in one direction, the driver may overtake on the right.

questions.question: A driver may overtake or pass on the right another vehicle that is doing what?
options: Making or about to make a left turn
Driving too slowly in the fast lane
questions.explanation: Nothing prohibits a driver from overtaking on the right another vehicle which is making or about to make a left turn.

questions.question: Overtaking is prohibited at which of the following locations?
options: At railway grade crossings and intersections unless controlled by traffic signal
On wide boulevards with light traffic
On roads with broken white lines
questions.explanation: The driver shall not overtake at any railway grade crossing or at any intersection of highways unless controlled by traffic signal.

questions.question: A driver shall not overtake between points indicated by official temporary signs that indicate what?
questions.explanation: Do not overtake between points indicated by official temporary signs indicating men are working on the highway.

questions.question: What does the No Overtaking Zone sign indicate?
options: Vehicles may overtake only on the left
Vehicles are not allowed to overtake or pass in that area
Overtaking is allowed only at night
questions.explanation: The No Overtaking Zone sign means vehicles are not allowed to overtake in that zone.

questions.question: Where should you NOT overtake according to driving safety rules?
options: At intersections, approaching a bridge or curve, solid lines, school zones, and railroad crossings
On highways with two or more lanes
When the vehicle ahead signals a left turn
questions.explanation: Do not overtake at intersections, approaching bridges/curves/crests, on solid lines, shoulders, railroads, hospital and school zones.

questions.question: On a two-lane road with normal traffic, overtaking is only allowed at which lane?
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, overtaking is only allowed at the left lane (first lane/leftmost).

questions.question: What should a motorcycle rider never do when overtaking?
options: Overtake on a curve especially on an uphill or downhill road
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders should never overtake on a curve especially on an uphill or downhill road.

questions.question: If you are hesitant to overtake the vehicle in front, what must you do?
questions.explanation: If hesitant to overtake, you must NOT overtake.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line prohibit a motorist from doing?
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line prohibits a motorist from overtaking.

questions.question: Is overtaking permitted if there are two solid yellow lines?
options: Yes, if the road ahead is clear
questions.explanation: Overtaking is NEVER permitted if there are two solid yellow lines.

questions.question: What should you do if another vehicle overtakes you?
options: Speed up to prevent them from passing
Stay with the current speed and do NOT attempt to race
questions.explanation: If another vehicle overtakes you, stay with current speed and do NOT attempt to race.

questions.question: When the vehicle in front does NOT give way, what must you do?
options: Be patient and do NOT overtake
questions.explanation: When the vehicle in front does not give way, be patient and do NOT overtake.

questions.question: On an expressway, which vehicles are NOT allowed in Lane No. 1 at all times?
options: Cargo trucks, buses, and slow-moving vehicles
questions.explanation: Cargo trucks, buses, and slow-moving vehicles are NOT allowed in Lane No. 1 at all times.

questions.question: On a one-way road, overtaking is permitted on which side?
options: Either on the right or the left lane if free from obstruction
questions.explanation: On a one-way road, overtaking is permitted either on the right or the left lane if free from obstruction.

questions.question: Never overtake a large hauling truck that is doing what?
questions.explanation: Never overtake a large hauling truck that is turning. It may block all or some lanes.

questions.question: When behind a longer vehicle, what must you do to improve visibility?
questions.explanation: When behind a longer vehicle, stay further back to improve your visibility.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider must never overtake a turning vehicle especially where?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders should never overtake a turning vehicle especially on its blind spots.

questions.question: When making a right turn, the driver should keep the rear right wheel nearest to what?
options: The curb or edge of the highway
questions.explanation: At the turn position, keep your rear right wheel nearest to the curb or edge of the highway.

questions.question: When making a left turn at an intersection, which lane should the driver turn into?
options: The lane nearest to the center line
questions.explanation: Make your left turn into the lane nearest to the center line.

questions.question: When stopped at an intersection waiting to make a left turn, how should you keep your wheels?
questions.explanation: If stopped, keep your wheels pointed straight ahead and wait to cross the intersection.

questions.question: Why is turning left more dangerous than turning right at an intersection?
options: Vehicles coming from the opposite direction are faster
Left turns have a wider turning radius
questions.explanation: Turning left is more dangerous because vehicles coming from the opposite direction are faster.

questions.question: When making a left turn from a one-way street to a two-way street, where should you position your vehicle?
options: In the center of the road
questions.explanation: Move towards the left-most lane and keep to the left-most lane while turning.

questions.question: When making a left turn from a one-way street to another one-way street, where should you position your vehicle?
options: Nearest to the curb upon reaching the intersection
In the middle of the road
questions.explanation: Position your vehicle nearest to the curb upon reaching the intersection when turning from one-way to one-way.

questions.question: When is a U-turn NOT permitted?
options: On a double solid yellow line and where a No U-Turn sign is posted
At an intersection with a traffic signal
On a road with broken white lines
questions.explanation: A U-turn is NOT permitted on a double solid yellow line and where a No U-Turn sign is posted.

questions.question: When making a U-turn, from which side should you start turning?
options: From the left side of the road
From the right side of the innermost lane
questions.explanation: Start a U-turn from the right side of the innermost lane.

questions.question: In making a U-turn on a motorcycle, it is NOT advisable to use which brake?
questions.explanation: In making a U-turn, it is NOT advisable to use the front wheel brake.

questions.question: Before making a U-turn, what should you check for?
options: Traffic in both directions and make the proper turn signal
questions.explanation: When doing a U-turn, check for traffic in both directions and make the proper turn signal.

questions.question: When making a turn on a red signal from a one-way street to a one-way street, what must you first check?
options: If the road is wide enough
If you are allowed to make a turn on a Red Signal
questions.explanation: First check if you are allowed to make a turn on a Red Signal. If yes, proceed safely. Otherwise, STOP and wait for green.

questions.question: Which lane should you stay on after turning right at an intersection?
questions.explanation: After turning right at the intersection, stay on the rightmost lane.

questions.question: When turning left, where should a motorcycle rider position the motorcycle?
options: Nearest to the center of the highway
questions.explanation: When turning left, the rider should position the motorcycle nearest to the center of the highway pursuant to R.A. No. 4136.

questions.question: Before making a U-turn, what must you do regarding traffic behind you?
options: Check traffic behind and indicate intention with a left turn signal
Speed up to avoid traffic behind
questions.explanation: Before a U-turn, check for traffic behind, indicate intention with a left turn signal, and give way to oncoming vehicles.

questions.question: What does a green arrow traffic light mean?
options: Vehicles turning in that direction shall proceed
questions.explanation: A green arrow means vehicles turning in that direction shall proceed.

questions.question: After making a left turn at an intersection, what should you do?
options: Immediately change to the right lane
Switch off the signal light and proceed to the proper lane with care
Speed up to merge with traffic
questions.explanation: After making a left turn, switch off the signal light and proceed to the proper lane with care.

questions.question: What should you do if you make a wrong turn on a one-way road?
options: Back up if possible or safely make a U-turn
Stop in the middle of the road
questions.explanation: If you make a wrong turn on a one-way road, back up if possible or safely make a U-turn.

questions.question: When making a right turn, what should a driver do after reducing to a safe speed?
questions.explanation: When making a right turn, reduce to a safe speed and signal your intention to turn.

questions.question: When parking downhill with a curb, how should the front wheels be turned?
options: Into the curb or toward the sidewalk
questions.explanation: When parking downhill or uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels into the curb or toward the sidewalk.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a road without a curb, the wheels should be turned toward which direction?
options: Toward the center of the road
Toward the edge of the road
questions.explanation: When parking uphill without a curb, turn wheels toward the edge of the road so the vehicle rolls away from the road if brakes fail.

questions.question: When parking uphill with a curb, which direction must the front wheels be turned?
questions.explanation: When parking uphill, turn your wheels away from the curb.

questions.question: No driver shall park a vehicle within how many meters of a fire hydrant?
questions.explanation: No driver shall park within four meters of a fire hydrant.

questions.question: Parking is prohibited within how many meters of the intersection of curb lines?
questions.explanation: No driver shall park within six meters of the intersection of curb lines.

questions.question: Parking is prohibited within how many meters of a driveway entrance to a fire station?
questions.explanation: No driver shall park within four meters of a driveway entrance to a fire station.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a prohibited parking location under R.A. No. 4136?
options: In front of a private driveway
questions.explanation: Prohibited locations include intersections, crosswalks, within 6m of curb lines, within 4m of fire stations/hydrants, in front of private driveways, and where signs prohibit.

questions.question: When angle parking is required, at what angle should vehicles be parked to the curb?
questions.explanation: Vehicles shall be parked at an angle of about forty-five degrees (45) to the curb.

questions.question: In angle parking, one front wheel must be within what distance of the curb?
questions.explanation: One of the front wheels must be touching or within one foot of the curb.

questions.question: A driver must not park or stop within what distance of a Stop sign or traffic control signal?
questions.explanation: Do not park or stop within six (6) meters of a Stop sign or traffic control signal.

questions.question: Can a motorist park in a pedestrian lane or crosswalk?
options: Yes, if only for a few minutes
Yes, if no pedestrians are present
questions.explanation: Parking in a pedestrian lane or crosswalk is never allowed under R.A. No. 4136.

questions.question: What does a Tow-Away Zone sign mean?
questions.explanation: A Tow-Away Zone means parked vehicles will be towed.

questions.question: What does the No Parking on Fire Hydrant sign indicate?
questions.explanation: The No Parking on Fire Hydrant sign indicates no waiting within 4 meters of a fire hydrant.

questions.question: On an expressway, where may a driver stop for an emergency?
questions.explanation: On expressways, you may stop for an emergency on the lay-by.

questions.question: A person is allowed to stop on an expressway only when instructed by whom?
questions.explanation: You are only allowed to stop on expressways when instructed by a traffic enforcer.

questions.question: You find a vacant PWD parking space but you are not a PWD. Can you park there?
options: Yes, if only for a few minutes
No, PWD parking spaces are intended only for PWDs
Yes, if no PWDs are visible
questions.explanation: PWD parking spaces are intended only for PWDs. You cannot park there at any time.

questions.question: Can you leave your motor vehicle while the engine is running at a complete stop on the road?
options: Yes, if the road is empty
Yes, if the parking brake is engaged
questions.explanation: Never leave a vehicle with engine running at a complete stop on the road. It may cause confusion and road crash.

questions.question: What must you always remember whenever you park?
options: Turn the engine off and put the proper stand
questions.explanation: Whenever you park, turn the engine off and put the proper stand.

questions.question: What hand signal must a driver give when wanting to stop?
options: Left arm held down and hand pointing to the ground
Left arm bent at elbow, hand pointing up
Right arm extended out the window
questions.explanation: The stop hand signal is left arm held down and hand pointing to the ground.

questions.question: What hand signal must a driver give when wanting to turn left?
options: Left arm bent at elbow, hand up
questions.explanation: The left turn hand signal is left arm held straight horizontally.

questions.question: What hand signal must a driver give when wanting to turn right?
options: Left arm bent at elbow, hand pointing up
questions.explanation: The right turn hand signal is left arm bent at the elbow, hand pointing up.

questions.question: According to R.A. No. 4136, the required signal shall be given by what means?
options: Extending hand and arm beyond the left side of the vehicle, or by approved mechanical or electrical signal device
Waving a flag out the window
questions.explanation: The signal shall be given by extending the hand and arm beyond the left side of the vehicle, or by an approved mechanical or electrical signal device.

questions.question: Turn signal lights are used for what purpose?
options: To make turning direction clear to other road users
questions.explanation: Turn signal lights make your turning direction clear to drivers and other road users.

questions.question: What should you do to warn the vehicle behind that you are slowing down or stopping?
options: Wave your hand out the window
Press on your brakes lightly to activate brake lights
questions.explanation: Press on your brakes lightly to activate brake lights to warn the vehicle behind.

questions.question: When riding in a motorcycle group, what is the correct hand signal for Follow Me?
options: Left hand straight up, palm forward
Right arm extended to the side
questions.explanation: The Follow Me signal for group riding is left hand straight up, palm forward.

questions.question: Can motorcycle riders use international hand signals not specified by Philippine law?
options: Yes, all hand signals are valid
Other international signs may be used for group riding only
No signals are needed for motorcycles
questions.explanation: Other international signs may be used for group riding only. Unrecognized signals are not lawful.

questions.question: What is the first thing to do when changing lanes?
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, you should first make a signal.

questions.question: Before starting, stopping or turning from a direct line, a driver shall first ensure what?
options: That such movement can be made in safety
That the fuel tank is full
questions.explanation: Before starting, stopping, or turning, first see that such movement can be made in safety.

questions.question: What does a steady RED traffic signal mean?
options: You must bring your vehicle to a STOP at a marked line
questions.explanation: RED SIGNAL means you must bring your vehicle to a STOP at a marked line.

questions.question: What does a FLASHING RED signal mean?
options: STOP and proceed only when it is safe
questions.explanation: FLASHING RED SIGNAL means bring your vehicle to a STOP and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a YELLOW or AMBER traffic signal indicate?
options: The RED signal is about to appear
questions.explanation: YELLOW/AMBER SIGNAL indicates that the RED signal is about to appear.

questions.question: What does a FLASHING YELLOW light mean?
options: Slow down and proceed with caution
questions.explanation: FLASHING YELLOW LIGHT means slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: What does a GREEN traffic signal mean?
options: You can proceed, provided you yield to pedestrians and traffic lawfully using the intersection
The signal is about to turn red
questions.explanation: GREEN SIGNAL means you can proceed, provided you yield to pedestrians and traffic lawfully using the intersection.

questions.question: What does a FLASHING GREEN signal mean?
options: Proceed with caution and be prepared for pedestrians who might cross
questions.explanation: FLASHING GREEN means proceed with caution and be prepared for pedestrians who might cross.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow arrow on a traffic light mean?
options: Turning vehicles must slow down and prepare to stop
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means turning vehicles facing the arrow must slow down and prepare to stop.

questions.question: At an intersection, what must all vehicles facing a steady red light do?
questions.explanation: All vehicles facing a steady red light must stop at the STOP line.

questions.question: What does beating the red light mean?
options: Passing through yellow lights coming to the intersection
questions.explanation: Beating the red light means passing through yellow lights coming to the intersection.

questions.question: When approaching a crossing or intersection, what should a driver do?
questions.explanation: A driver approaching a crossing or intersection shall slow down and stop.

questions.question: What does a red X light or sign at a toll gate mean?
options: You cannot drive through this lane
questions.explanation: A red X light/sign at a toll gate means you cannot drive through this lane.

questions.question: What should you do when crossing a railroad with NO warning devices?
options: Slow down, check both sides, proceed with caution if clear
questions.explanation: Slow down, check both sides of the road, then proceed with caution if clear (stop, look and listen).

questions.question: Before traversing a through highway or railroad crossing, what must a driver do?
options: Bring the vehicle to a full stop, or slow to five miles per hour if no hazard exists
questions.explanation: Bring to a full stop before traversing a through highway or railroad crossing. If no hazard exists, slow to five miles per hour.

questions.question: When must you make a complete or full stop at an intersection?
questions.explanation: A complete/full stop is required at a red traffic light.

questions.question: When turning left from one highway to another, where must the vehicle be conducted?
options: To the right of the center of the intersection
questions.explanation: When turning left from one highway to another, every vehicle shall be conducted to the right of the center of the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do if you entered the wrong lane at a busy junction?
options: Continue in that lane until safe to return to the proper lane
questions.explanation: Continue driving in that lane until it is safe to return to the proper lane.

questions.question: When entering a roundabout, what must the driver do?
options: Yield the right-of-way to vehicles already inside
questions.explanation: Yield the right-of-way to vehicles already inside the roundabout.

questions.question: A flashing red light indicates that you should do what?
options: Stop, yield, and proceed when safe
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop, yield, and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does an orange traffic sign mean?
options: Roadwork ahead, follow prescribed speed limit
questions.explanation: An orange traffic sign means roadwork ahead; follow the prescribed speed limit.

questions.question: What shape is a Stop sign?
questions.explanation: The shape of a Stop sign is an octagon.

questions.question: What does a yellow traffic light mean and what is disregarding it called?
options: Slow down and prepare to stop; beating the red light
questions.explanation: Yellow means slow down and prepare to stop. Disregarding it constitutes beating the red light, tantamount to reckless driving.

questions.question: Which vehicles have the right-of-way at a rotunda or roundabout?
questions.explanation: The vehicles within the roundabout have the right-of-way.

questions.question: What should you do before exiting a roundabout?
options: Signal your intention and check your side mirror
questions.explanation: Signal your intention and check your side mirror before you exit the roundabout.

questions.question: Unless safety requires otherwise, on which side must a driver pass when meeting oncoming vehicles?
questions.explanation: Every person operating a motor vehicle shall pass to the right when meeting oncoming vehicles.

questions.question: When overtaking vehicles going the same direction, on which side must a driver pass?
questions.explanation: Pass to the left when overtaking persons or vehicles going the same direction.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence for changing lanes?
options: Check traffic, mirrors, blind spots, signal ON, steer, signal OFF
questions.explanation: Check traffic ahead/behind/sides, check mirrors, glance at blind spots, switch ON signal, steer into new lane, switch OFF signal.

questions.question: On an expressway, what is the minimum speed limit?
questions.explanation: Expressway speed limits: minimum 60 kph, maximum 100 kph.

questions.question: On an expressway, what is the maximum speed limit for light vehicles?
questions.explanation: The expressway maximum speed limit for light vehicles is 100 kph.

questions.question: On an expressway with four lanes in each direction, which lane is for overtaking only?
questions.explanation: Lane 1 (innermost) is used only for overtaking within the allowed speed.

questions.question: When merging onto an expressway, you should make full use of which lane?
questions.explanation: When merging on expressway, make full use of the acceleration lane (continuity lane).

questions.question: In which lane should you merge onto the expressway?
questions.explanation: When merging on the expressway, take the rightmost lane.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow or white line on the road mean?
options: Passing or overtaking is NOT allowed
questions.explanation: A solid yellow or white line means passing/overtaking is NOT allowed.

questions.question: What does a broken white line between lanes mean?
options: Overtaking or changing lane allowed if safe
questions.explanation: A white broken line means overtaking or changing lane is allowed if it is safe.

questions.question: On a two-way road, what does a single white broken line mean?
options: It separates traffic moving in opposite directions
questions.explanation: A single white broken line separates traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: What do double yellow solid lines mean?
questions.explanation: Double yellow solid lines mean no crossing or overtaking.

questions.question: On a single solid yellow line, when are you allowed to cross?
options: Only when turning into a driveway
questions.explanation: On a single solid yellow line, you are allowed to cross only when turning into a driveway.

questions.question: What do broken yellow lines allow motorists to do?
options: Overtake and cross when it is safe
questions.explanation: Broken yellow lines allow motorists to overtake and cross when it is safe.

questions.question: Is driving a private vehicle on a yellow bus lane allowed?
options: No, except when turning or entering garage within 100 meters
questions.explanation: Private vehicles are not allowed on yellow bus lanes, except when turning or going into a garage within 100 meters.

questions.question: What is the consequence of habitual and unnecessary lane changing for motorcycle riders?
options: It is tantamount to reckless driving
questions.explanation: Habitual and unnecessary changing of lane is tantamount to reckless driving.

questions.question: What should you do if on the leftmost lane of a multi-lane road you see signs of a closed road ahead?
options: Move to the other lane with care
questions.explanation: If you see signs of a closed road ahead while on the leftmost lane, move to the other lane with care.

questions.question: While driving on a street with no pavement markings, what should you do?
options: Proceed with caution and drive at the rightmost side
Use any part of the road
questions.explanation: On streets with no pavement markings, proceed with caution and drive at the rightmost side.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed for cars and motorcycles on open country roads with no blind corners?
questions.explanation: On open country roads with no blind corners, the max speed for cars and motorcycles is 80 km per hour.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed for cars on through streets or boulevards clear of traffic with no blind corners?
questions.explanation: On through streets or boulevards, the maximum speed for cars is 40 km per hour.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit on city and municipal streets with light traffic not designated as through streets?
questions.explanation: On city and municipal streets with light traffic, the maximum speed is 30 km per hour.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed through crowded streets, blind corners, school zones, or when passing stationary vehicles?
questions.explanation: Through crowded streets, blind corners, school zones, or passing stationary vehicles, the maximum speed is 20 km per hour.

questions.question: On national primary roads with flat topography, what is the recommended design speed under DPWH guidelines?
questions.explanation: For national primary roads with flat topography, the recommended design speed is 80 kph.

questions.question: On national secondary roads with mountainous topography, what is the recommended design speed?
questions.explanation: For national secondary roads with mountainous topography, the recommended design speed is 40 kph.

questions.question: On provincial open roads, what is the maximum speed for cars and motorcycles?
questions.explanation: On provincial open roads, the max speed for cars and motorcycles is 40 kph.

questions.question: On provincial crowded streets, what is the maximum speed for all vehicles?
questions.explanation: On provincial crowded streets, the max speed for all vehicles is 20 kph.

questions.question: Which of the following is an exception to speed restrictions under R.A. No. 4136?
options: A physician responding to emergency calls
questions.explanation: A physician or his driver responding to emergency calls is exempted from speed restrictions.

questions.question: How many specific exceptions to speed restrictions are listed under R.A. No. 4136?
questions.explanation: R.A. No. 4136 lists seven exceptions: physician, ambulance, wounded/sick transport, Armed Forces, pursuing criminals, law enforcement, and fire department.

questions.question: What is the two or three second rule used for?
options: Maintaining a safe following distance at any speed
questions.explanation: The two or three second rule is for maintaining a safe distance at any speed. It is a guide to reaction time.

questions.question: At 100 kph on full brake in ideal conditions, what is the braking distance?
questions.explanation: A vehicle at 100 kph in ideal conditions can travel 60 meters when applying full brake.

questions.question: At 100 kph, what is the total stopping distance on a full brake?
questions.explanation: A vehicle at 100 kph has a total stopping distance of 80 meters on a full brake.

questions.question: What is the perception distance for a vehicle running at 100 kph?
questions.explanation: A vehicle running at 100 kph has a perception distance of 20 meters.

questions.question: When should you use the horn according to law?
options: When a pedestrian or other vehicle may be affected by your movement
questions.explanation: The horn is used to give a clearly audible signal when a pedestrian or other vehicle may be affected by starting, stopping, or turning.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a motor vehicles horn?
options: To warn other road users of your presence
questions.explanation: A motor vehicles horn is used to warn other road users of your presence.

questions.question: A driver must not park or stop within what distance of a traffic light ahead sign?
questions.explanation: Do not park or stop within six (6) meters of a traffic light ahead sign, as it reduces visibility for other drivers.

questions.question: When stopped by a law enforcement officer, where should you safely pull over?
options: To the center of the road
questions.explanation: If stopped by an enforcer, safely pull over to the extreme right.

questions.question: When stopped by an enforcer, what should you do while in the vehicle?
options: Stay in the drivers seat, keep hands visible, follow officers instructions
questions.explanation: Stay in the drivers seat, do not get out unless asked, keep hands visible, and follow instructions.

questions.question: During an apprehension, a driver has the right to know what about the apprehending officer?
questions.explanation: All drivers are entitled to know the complete name and agency of the Apprehending Traffic Officer.

questions.question: To avoid suspension, within how many days must a driver settle their apprehension?
questions.explanation: The driver must settle their apprehension within 15 days pursuant to R.A. No. 4136 and JAO-2014-01.

questions.question: What documents should a driver carry at all times when driving?
options: Drivers License, Certificate of Registration, and current OR/CR
questions.explanation: A driver should carry Drivers License, Certificate of Registration, and current Official Receipt (OR/CR).

questions.question: If cargo extends beyond one meter from the vehicle body, what must you do?
options: Hang a red flag of at least 30x30 cm at the edge of the load
questions.explanation: Hang a red flag with at least 30x30 centimeters at the edge of the load. At night, replace with red light visible at least 50 meters away.

questions.question: What is the minimum engine displacement for a motorcycle allowed on expressways?
questions.explanation: Motorcycles below 400 cc are not allowed on expressways. The allowable displacement is 400cc and above.

questions.question: Which of the following vehicles is NOT allowed to enter expressways?
options: Motorcycles below 400 cc, tricycles, scooters, and bicycles
questions.explanation: Motorcycles below 400 cc, tricycles, scooters, and bicycles are not allowed on expressways.

questions.question: What should you NOT do in case of tire blowout or flat tire on the expressway?
questions.explanation: Do not slam on the brake in case of tire blowout or flat tire on the expressway.

questions.question: Under R.A. No. 11229, a child of what age and below cannot sit in the back seat without a child restraint system?
questions.explanation: Under R.A. No. 11229, a child 12 years old and below must use a child restraint system.

questions.question: What is the maximum permitted speed when driving within a school zone?
questions.explanation: When driving within the school zone, the maximum permitted speed is 20 kph.

questions.question: What should you do if a school service is parked on the other side with hazard warning lights on?
options: Slow down and prepare to stop, students are expected to cross
questions.explanation: Slow down and prepare to stop because students are expected to cross the street.

questions.question: When approaching a crest of a hill, what should you do?
options: Prepare to slow down and stay on your lane
questions.explanation: When approaching a crest, prepare to slow down and stay on your lane for safer travel.

questions.question: Under R.A. No. 10913, how may one legally use a mobile phone while driving?
options: Use a hands-free device such as Bluetooth or earpiece
Phones cannot be used at all
questions.explanation: Under the Anti-Distracted Driving Act, mobile phone use is permitted only with a hands-free device.

questions.question: If you need to use your mobile phone while driving, what should you do?
options: Stop at a safe side of the road
Use it only when traffic is light
questions.explanation: Stop at a safe side of the road to answer or make a call.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle at night, what type of clothing is advisable?
questions.explanation: Use bright clothing when riding at night to project clear visibility to other motorists.

questions.question: What is the allowable color of a motorcycle headlight?
questions.explanation: The allowable color of a motorcycle headlight is yellowish white or yellow.

questions.question: What is the mandatory blood alcohol content limit for motorcyclists?
questions.explanation: A motorcyclist must not exceed 0.00 percent Blood Alcohol Content when driving.

questions.question: What is the maximum penalty for violating R.A. No. 10666, the Childrens Safety on Motorcycle Act?
questions.explanation: The maximum penalty for violating R.A. No. 10666 is revocation of drivers license.

questions.question: Under R.A. No. 10666, what exemption allows a child to back ride on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: A child may back ride when they need to be transported to a hospital for immediate medical attention.

questions.question: What are the maximum dimensions for a customized motorcycle top box?
questions.explanation: The allowable maximum size is 2 feet x 2 feet x 2 feet and can fit two full-face helmets.

questions.question: What is the prescribed width limit for motorcycle saddle bags?
options: No more than 14 inches from the sides
questions.explanation: Saddle bags must follow a width of no more than 14 inches from the sides.

questions.question: What is the allowable number of bulbs for every auxiliary lamp (LED) on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The allowable number of bulbs for every auxiliary lamp (LED) is six (6).

questions.question: What is the color of a motorcycle brake light?
questions.explanation: The color of a motorcycle brake light must be bright red.

questions.question: Before starting the engine of a manual clutch vehicle, what gear position should it be in?
questions.explanation: For manual clutch vehicles, be sure the gear is in neutral position before starting.

questions.question: What should motorcycle riders avoid doing when starting the engine?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders should avoid pushing the motorcycle to start the engine.

questions.question: What is the recommended hand grip position on the steering wheel for good control?
questions.explanation: Hands grip the steering wheel at a 9:3 or 10:2 position for full control.

questions.question: When a vehicle stalls due to breakdown, where should the Early Warning Device (EWD) be placed?
options: 4 meters at the front and 4 meters at the rear
questions.explanation: Put the EWD at 4 meters at the front and 4 meters at the rear of the stalled vehicle.

questions.question: For safety, what must a motorcycle rider do with the headlights when riding?
questions.explanation: For safety reasons, SWITCH ON the headlights when riding the motorcycle.

questions.question: What proves a motorcycle helmet is within quality standards?
options: ICC or PS stickers attached at the back
questions.explanation: ICC or PS stickers attached at the back of the helmet prove it is within quality standards.

questions.question: What is the maximum penalty for driving under the influence of liquor or prohibited drugs?
questions.explanation: The maximum penalty for DUI is perpetual forfeiture of drivers license.

questions.question: What are the effects of alcohol on a driver?
options: Poor coordination and lack of self-judgment
questions.explanation: Alcohol causes poor coordination of body movements, lack of self-judgment, and slows reaction time.

questions.question: What should a driver do when taking medication that can affect driving?
options: Do NOT drive or consult a doctor
questions.explanation: When under medication affecting driving, do NOT drive or consult a doctor before driving.

questions.question: What is the acronym for the proper vehicle inspection a responsible driver must conduct?
questions.explanation: A responsible driver must conduct BLOWBAGETS/BLOWBAGA inspection for roadworthy and emission-compliant vehicles.

questions.question: Which of these is a prohibited driving act that could place your life at risk?
options: Using a mobile phone while driving
questions.explanation: Using a mobile phone while driving is prohibited as it distracts attention (R.A. No. 10913).

questions.question: When driving on expressways, how far ahead of the exit toll should you plan?
questions.explanation: Plan at least 1 km ahead of the exit toll on expressways.

questions.question: What does R.A. No. 8750, the Seat Belt Law, require?
options: Only the driver wears a seat belt
Mandatory use of seat belts as indicated by the Use Seat Belt sign
questions.explanation: The Use Seat Belt sign is used pursuant to R.A. No. 8750, mandating seat belt use.

questions.question: What is the additional penalty for NOT wearing a seatbelt on the third offense?
options: Suspension of drivers license for one (1) week
questions.explanation: The third offense penalty is suspension of drivers license for one (1) week per JAO-2014-01.

questions.question: When driving on a wet road, what should a driver do?
options: Slow down and take necessary precaution
questions.explanation: While driving on a wet road, slow down and take necessary precaution.

questions.question: Why should slam braking be avoided on a wet road?
options: Wheels may skid causing loss of steering control
questions.explanation: Slam braking on a wet road may cause wheels to skid and loss of steering control.

questions.question: Before driving on a steep downhill road, what must the driver do?
options: Shift to low gear to control speed
questions.explanation: Before driving on a steep downhill, shift to low gear to control the speed of the vehicle.

questions.question: While driving downhill, how can you preserve your brakes?
questions.explanation: While driving downhill, preserve your brakes by using the engine brake.

questions.question: On a long drive, what should you do if you are tired or sleepy?
options: Take a rest at a safe place and take a few minutes nap
Open the windows and drive faster
questions.explanation: On a long drive, park at a rest stop and take a few minutes nap if tired or sleepy.

questions.question: What should you do when following a student-driver?
options: Be patient, expect them to make mistakes
questions.explanation: When following a student-driver, be patient and expect them to make mistakes.

questions.question: In a road crash involving a pedestrian, what should you do?
options: Stop, assess the situation, provide appropriate help
questions.explanation: Stop and assess the situation, then provide appropriate help. Never touch unconscious or injured persons.

questions.question: Which of the following is an act considered as road rage?
questions.explanation: Tailgating is one of the acts considered road rage, along with cutting off, rude gestures, and annoying horn blowing.

questions.question: Which common PUV violation involves stopping outside of the designated zone?
options: Stopping outside the stopping zone and ignoring other motorists right-of-way
questions.explanation: A common PUV violation is stopping outside the stopping zone for loading/unloading passengers and ignoring other motorists right-of-way.

questions.question: What violation is committed when a driver opens the vehicle door while the vehicle is in motion?
questions.explanation: Opening the door while the vehicle is in motion is listed as a common traffic violation.

questions.question: What is lane straddling?
options: Driving with wheels on two lanes simultaneously, a common traffic violation
questions.explanation: Lane straddling is listed as a common traffic violation of public utility vehicle drivers.

questions.question: What is counterflowing?
options: Driving against the flow of traffic
questions.explanation: Counterflowing or driving against the flow of traffic is a common traffic violation.

questions.question: Stopping on a yellow box is considered what?
questions.explanation: Stopping on a yellow box is listed as a common traffic violation of public utility vehicle drivers.

questions.question: Under R.A. No. 4136, what is the maximum speed limit for cars and motorcycles on open country roads with no blind corners and not closely bordered by habitations?
questions.explanation: Section 35(B) of R.A. No. 4136 prescribes 80 km per hour for passenger cars and motorcycles on open country roads with no blind corners not closely bordered by habitations.

questions.question: Under R.A. No. 4136, what is the maximum speed limit for motor trucks and buses on open country roads?
questions.explanation: Section 35(B) of R.A. No. 4136 prescribes 50 km per hour for motor trucks and buses on open country roads with no blind corners.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed for cars and motorcycles on designated through streets or boulevards clear of traffic with no blind corners?
questions.explanation: R.A. No. 4136 Section 35(B) prescribes 40 km per hour for cars and motorcycles on through streets or boulevards clear of traffic with no blind corners.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed for motor trucks and buses on designated through streets or boulevards?
questions.explanation: R.A. No. 4136 Section 35(B) prescribes 30 km per hour for motor trucks and buses on through streets or boulevards clear of traffic with no blind corners.

questions.question: Under R.A. No. 4136, what is the maximum speed limit on city and municipal streets with light traffic when not designated as through streets?
questions.explanation: R.A. No. 4136 Section 35(B) prescribes 30 km per hour for all vehicles on city and municipal streets with light traffic not designated as through streets.

questions.question: Under R.A. No. 4136, what is the maximum speed limit when passing through crowded streets, approaching intersections at blind corners, or passing school zones?
questions.explanation: R.A. No. 4136 Section 35(B) prescribes 20 km per hour for crowded streets, approaching intersections at blind corners, passing school zones, and similar dangerous circumstances.

questions.question: Which law specifies the general prescribed rate of speed limits in the Philippines?
questions.explanation: The prescribed rate of speed is specified under Section 35(B) of Republic Act No. 4136.

questions.question: Under R.A. No. 4136 speed limits, cars and motorcycles share the same maximum speed as motor trucks and buses on which type of road?
questions.explanation: On city and municipal streets with light traffic, both cars/motorcycles and motor trucks/buses are limited to 30 km per hour under R.A. No. 4136.

questions.question: Which has a higher maximum speed limit under R.A. No. 4136: open country roads or through streets?
options: It depends on the vehicle type
questions.explanation: Open country roads allow 80 kph for cars and 50 kph for trucks/buses, while through streets allow only 40 kph and 30 kph respectively.

questions.question: What is the recommended design speed for a primary national road with flat topography under DPWH guidelines?
questions.explanation: Under Joint Memorandum Circular 2018-001 and DPWH design guidelines, primary national roads with flat topography have a recommended design speed of 80 kph.

questions.question: What is the recommended design speed for a primary national road with rolling topography?
questions.explanation: Under Joint Memorandum Circular 2018-001, primary national roads with rolling topography have a recommended design speed of 60 kph.

questions.question: What is the recommended design speed for a primary national road with mountainous topography?
questions.explanation: Under Joint Memorandum Circular 2018-001, primary national roads with mountainous topography have a recommended design speed of 50 kph.

questions.question: What is the recommended design speed for a secondary national road with flat topography?
questions.explanation: Under Joint Memorandum Circular 2018-001, secondary national roads with flat topography have a recommended design speed of 70 kph.

questions.question: What is the recommended design speed for a secondary national road with rolling topography?
questions.explanation: Under Joint Memorandum Circular 2018-001, secondary national roads with rolling topography have a recommended design speed of 60 kph.

questions.question: What is the recommended design speed for a secondary national road with mountainous topography?
questions.explanation: Under Joint Memorandum Circular 2018-001, secondary national roads with mountainous topography have a recommended design speed of 40 kph.

questions.question: Which government agencies jointly issued the memorandum circular on national road speed limits in 2018?
questions.explanation: Joint Memorandum Circular 2018-001 dated 17 January 2018 was issued by DOTr, DPWH, and DILG.

questions.question: According to the source, what takes precedence when a speed limit sign is posted on a road?
options: The posted speed limit on the road
questions.explanation: The FDM states that the speed limit posted on the road shall prevail over the general prescribed rates.

questions.question: According to the reviewer, what is the maximum speed limit on the national road under the law?
questions.explanation: The reviewer states that the maximum speed limit on the national road under R.A. No. 4136 is 80 km/hr.

questions.question: At what maximum speed may cars and motorcycles travel on a secondary national road with flat topography?
questions.explanation: Secondary national roads with flat topography have a recommended design speed of 70 kph under JMC 2018-001.

questions.question: What is the lowest recommended design speed among all categories of national roads?
questions.explanation: The lowest recommended design speed for national roads is 40 kph, which applies to secondary national roads with mountainous topography.

questions.question: Under R.A. No. 4136, what is the speed limit for all vehicles on crowded streets?
questions.explanation: R.A. No. 4136 prescribes 20 km per hour on crowded streets, approaching intersections at blind corners, and similar dangerous circumstances.

questions.question: What is the speed limit for cars and motorcycles on through streets or boulevards designated as such?
questions.explanation: R.A. No. 4136 prescribes 40 km per hour for cars and motorcycles on designated through streets or boulevards clear of traffic with no blind corners.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed for motor trucks and buses on through streets?
questions.explanation: R.A. No. 4136 prescribes 30 km per hour for motor trucks and buses on through streets or boulevards.

questions.question: Under the DPWH provincial road speed limits, what is the maximum speed for cars and motorcycles on a provincial open road?
questions.explanation: Under DPWH Memorandum April 14, 2014, the maximum speed for passenger cars and motorcycles on provincial open roads is 40 kph.

questions.question: Under DPWH provincial road speed limits, what is the maximum speed for motor trucks and buses on a provincial open road?
questions.explanation: Under DPWH Memorandum April 14, 2014, motor trucks and buses on provincial open roads are limited to 30 kph.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed on a provincial crowded street for all vehicle types?
questions.explanation: Under DPWH Memorandum April 14, 2014, all vehicles on provincial crowded streets are limited to 20 kph.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed for cars on municipal or city streets under the DPWH provincial road speed limits?
questions.explanation: Under DPWH Memorandum April 14, 2014, passenger cars and motorcycles on municipal or city streets are limited to 30 kph.

questions.question: What is the speed limit on barangay roads under the DPWH provincial road speed limits?
questions.explanation: Under DPWH Memorandum April 14, 2014, all vehicles on municipal or city barangay roads are limited to 20 kph.

questions.question: On provincial through streets under DPWH rules, what are the speed limits for cars and for trucks/buses respectively?
questions.explanation: Under DPWH Memorandum April 14, 2014, provincial through streets allow 40 kph for cars/motorcycles and 30 kph for motor trucks/buses.

questions.question: Under DPWH provincial road rules, which road classification has the same 20 kph limit for both cars and trucks?
questions.explanation: Under DPWH Memorandum April 14, 2014, both crowded streets and barangay roads have a uniform 20 kph limit for all vehicle types.

questions.question: Under R.A. No. 4136, at what maximum speed can a bus travel on a city or municipal street that is not a designated through street?
questions.explanation: On city and municipal streets with light traffic not designated as through streets, motor trucks and buses are limited to 30 km per hour under R.A. No. 4136.

questions.question: Under which conditions does R.A. No. 4136 allow a through street designation with a 40 kph limit?
options: Clear of traffic, with no blind corners, when so designated
questions.explanation: R.A. No. 4136 specifies that through streets must be clear of traffic, have no blind corners, and be so designated to qualify for the 40 kph limit.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit when passing through a school zone?
questions.explanation: Under R.A. No. 4136, passing through school zones falls under the 20 km per hour limit along with crowded streets and blind corners.

questions.question: When driving within a school zone, what is the maximum permitted speed according to the reviewer?
questions.explanation: The reviewer states that the maximum permitted speed within the school zone is 20 kph, pursuant to R.A. No. 4136.

questions.question: Under R.A. No. 4136, the speed limit in school zones is the same as the limit for which other condition?
questions.explanation: R.A. No. 4136 groups school zones together with crowded streets, blind corners, and passing stationary vehicles under the same 20 kph limit.

questions.question: What should a driver do when a school service vehicle is parked on the other side of the highway with its hazard warning lights on?
options: Slow down and prepare to stop
questions.explanation: The reviewer advises that when a school service is parked with hazard lights on, students are expected to cross the street, so drivers must slow down and prepare to stop.

questions.question: Which supplementary traffic sign is specifically associated with schools and playgrounds?
questions.explanation: The road signs section lists a supplementary sign for schools and playground, along with signs for PWDs and senior citizens.

questions.question: Under R.A. No. 4136, what speed limit applies to both a passenger car and a bus when passing a school zone?
options: 20 kph for the car, 15 kph for the bus
30 kph for the car, 20 kph for the bus
questions.explanation: R.A. No. 4136 prescribes 20 km per hour for all vehicles when passing school zones, with no distinction between vehicle types.

questions.explanation: It is advisable to use bright clothing when riding a motorcycle at night to project clear visibility from other motorists.

questions.question: What is the prescribed color of a motorcycle headlight?
questions.explanation: The allowable color of motorcycle headlight is yellowish white or yellow.

questions.question: What color must a motorcycle brake light be?
questions.explanation: The color of brake light for motorcycle must be bright red.

questions.question: If cargo exceeds one meter from the body of your vehicle at night, what must you do?
options: Attach a red light that is visible at least 50 meters away
Attach a white flag to the load
questions.explanation: If your cargo exceeded one meter from the body of your vehicle, at night the red flag must be replaced with a red light that is visible at least 50 meters away.

questions.question: What should you do if you want to slow down or stop to communicate your intention to drivers behind you?
options: Press on your brakes lightly to activate brake lights
Wave your hand out the window
questions.explanation: If you want to slow down or stop, press on your brakes lightly to activate brake lights.

questions.question: What is a blind spot?
options: The area directly in front of the vehicle
The area to your right or left that you do not see on the side view mirror
The area directly behind the vehicle seen in the rearview mirror
questions.explanation: The blind spot is the area to your right or left that you do not see on the side view mirror.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do after checking the rearview and side mirrors?
options: Immediately steer into the new lane
Take a quick glance on the blind spots
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, after checking the rearview mirror and side mirrors, take a quick glance on the blind spots before switching on the signal light and steering into the new lane.

questions.question: What is the risk of driving alongside a car on a motorcycle?
options: It is prone to road crash due to blind spots
It makes the motorcycle more visible
questions.explanation: The risk of driving alongside a car is that it is prone to road crash due to blind spots.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist never overtake a turning vehicle?
options: Because it is illegal at all times
Because of the blind spots, especially on large vehicles like buses and trucks
Because it consumes too much fuel
Because the road is always too narrow
questions.explanation: Never overtake a turning vehicle especially on its blind spots. Large vehicles such as buses and trucks have more blind spots than cars and jeepneys.

questions.question: What will you do before reversing to check your blind spots?
options: Look around to see that the way is clear
Close your eyes and proceed slowly
questions.explanation: Before you reverse, look around to see that the way is clear because the blind spot is the area you do not see on the side view mirror.

questions.question: During backing up, what directional checks must you perform?
options: Only look through the rear window
Make quick checks over left and right shoulder and look through the mirror or rear window
Only look at the side mirror
questions.explanation: Make quick checks over left and right shoulder and look through the mirror or rear window.

questions.question: What is the main problem when reversing that results in road crashes?
questions.explanation: The main problem when reversing is poor visibility resulting to road crashes.

questions.question: What is the first thing you should do when the brake fails on a vehicle not equipped with ABS?
options: Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times to build brake fluid pressure
questions.explanation: When the brake fails, rapidly pump the brake pedal several times to build brake fluid pressure. But for the car equipped with an anti-lock braking system, do not pump the brake.

questions.question: During a tire blowout, what should you avoid doing?
options: Taking your foot off the accelerator pedal
Holding on to the steering wheel
questions.explanation: In a tire blowout, do not slam on the brakes. Instead, take your foot off the accelerator pedal, hold on to the steering wheel, and slow down gradually.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of actions during a tire blowout?
options: Slam brakes, then steer to the side, then turn on hazards
Take foot off accelerator, do not slam brakes, hold steering wheel, slow down gradually, apply brake softly when under control, pull to safe side
Accelerate to stabilize, then brake hard, then park
Turn off engine, coast to a stop, then restart
questions.explanation: For a tire blowout: take your foot off the accelerator pedal, do not slam on the brakes, hold on to the steering wheel, slow down gradually, apply the brake softly whenever the vehicle is under control, and pull the vehicle to the safe side of the road.

questions.question: What should you do if the gas pedal becomes jammed?
options: Release the accelerator pedal, shift to neutral, firmly press the brake pedal, and do not shut off the engine
Keep pressing the accelerator to unjam it
Pull the parking brake as hard as possible
questions.explanation: For a jammed gas pedal: release the accelerator pedal, shift to neutral, firmly press the brake pedal to slow the vehicle, and do not shut off the engine because you may lose the ability to steer.

questions.question: Why should you not shut off the engine when the gas pedal is jammed?
options: Because you may lose the ability to steer the vehicle
Because the air conditioner will stop working
Because the radio will turn off
questions.explanation: Do not shut off the engine when the gas pedal is jammed because you may lose the ability to steer the vehicle.

questions.question: What is the first thing you should do after a road crash?
questions.explanation: In a road crash, the first action is to stop. Then turn on hazard flashers, check yourself and passengers, take photos, and call law enforcement.

questions.question: When a vehicle is submerged in water, approximately how long will it float on the surface?
questions.explanation: The vehicle will only float on the surface for about 30 to 60 seconds if you crash in a river or other bodies of water.

questions.question: What type of fire extinguisher should be used for vehicle fires?
questions.explanation: In case of vehicle fire, use appropriate fire extinguisher (ABC). Do not put water on diesel or gasoline.

questions.question: Why should you not put water on a diesel or gasoline fire?
options: Because water is too expensive to waste
Because water may cause the fuel fire to spread
Because water is not available on the road
questions.explanation: In case of fire, do not put water on diesel or gasoline. Use appropriate fire extinguisher (ABC).

questions.question: What is the primary responsibility of a driver who has been involved in a road crash?
options: Assess the situation, assist the injured person if possible, and call for help
Wait for the other driver to act first
questions.explanation: The primary responsibility of a driver who has been involved in a road crash is to assess the situation and if possible, assist the injured person and call for help.

questions.question: In a road crash involving a pedestrian, what should you never do?
options: Attempt to touch an unconscious or injured person
questions.explanation: In a road crash involving a pedestrian, never attempt to touch unconscious or injured person. Stop and assess the situation, then provide appropriate help.

questions.question: How do you use an Early Warning Device (EWD) when stalled due to motor vehicle breakdown?
options: Put the EWD at 2 meters front and 2 meters rear
Put the EWD at a distance of 4 meters at the front and 4 meters at the rear of the stalled vehicle
Put the EWD only at the rear of the vehicle
Put the EWD at 10 meters front and 10 meters rear
questions.explanation: Put the EWD at a distance of 4 meters at the front and 4 meters at the rear of the stalled vehicle.

questions.question: On expressways, where may you stop to attend or call for an emergency?
options: In the middle of any lane
questions.explanation: When driving on expressways, you may stop to attend or call for an emergency on the lay-by.

questions.question: When are you allowed to stop on expressways?
options: Whenever you need to check your phone
When instructed by a traffic enforcer
questions.explanation: You are only allowed to stop on expressways when instructed by a traffic enforcer.

questions.question: When should you switch on your hazard warning lights on an expressway?
questions.explanation: Expressway driving tip number 9 states: switch on hazard warning light only when stopping for emergencies.

questions.question: What additional actions should you take if you cannot slow your vehicle during brake failure?
options: Close your eyes and brace for impact
Sound your horn and flash your lights to alarm pedestrians or other motorists
Turn off the engine and coast
Open the doors to create drag
questions.explanation: When the brake fails, sound your horn and flash your lights if you cannot slow your vehicle to alarm pedestrians or other motorists.

questions.question: How should you use the parking brake when the main brakes fail?
options: Pull it suddenly and with full force
Sporadically use the parking brake to slow down the vehicle
Never use the parking brake during brake failure
Only use it after the vehicle has completely stopped
questions.explanation: When the brake fails, sporadically use the parking brake to slow down the vehicle.

questions.question: What is the purpose of rumble strips across the road?
options: To make you alert and be aware of your speed
questions.explanation: The rumble strips across the road is intended to make you alert and be aware of your speed.

questions.question: What are fixed hazards on the road?
options: Hazards that change throughout the day
Structures along the roadway that may restrict your vision such as curves, hills, and hidden driveways
Only road signs that are broken
questions.explanation: Fixed hazards are structures along the roadway that may restrict your vision in areas such as curves, hills and hidden driveways, intersections, and merging roadways.

questions.question: What are dynamic hazards on the road?
options: Hazards that may change through the day such as school zones and market areas
questions.explanation: Dynamic hazards are hazards that may change through the day such as school zones, market areas, and other commercial districts. These also include emergency vehicles.

questions.question: What does an orange traffic sign mean?
options: There is roadwork ahead and you must follow the prescribed speed limit
There is a school zone ahead
questions.explanation: An orange traffic sign means there is roadwork ahead and you must follow the prescribed speed limit.

questions.question: What should you do upon entering a roadwork with a temporary maximum speed limit sign?
options: Ignore the sign and maintain your speed
Comply with the sign at all times and drive at a maximum speed of 40 kph
Only slow down if workers are present
Speed up to leave the area faster
questions.explanation: Upon entering a roadwork with a temporary maximum speed limit sign, you must comply with the sign at all times and drive at a maximum speed of 40 kph.

questions.question: If your front wheel drops off the pavement, what should you do after slowing down?
options: Immediately steer sharply back onto the road
Keep your vehicle on a straight course, check for opening in traffic, and steer slowly back onto the pavement at a slight angle
Accelerate to jump back onto the road
Turn the wheel fully in the opposite direction
questions.explanation: For pavement drop-off: slow down to a safe speed, keep your vehicle on a straight course, check for opening in traffic and steer slowly back onto the pavement at a slight angle. Then straighten the wheel position immediately as the front wheels contact the pavement.

questions.question: When diesel fuel or oil is spilled on the road, it is dangerous to all motorists, particularly whom?
questions.explanation: When diesel fuel or oil is spilled on the road, it is dangerous to all motorists, particularly motorcyclists.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no warning devices, what should you do?
options: Slow down, check both sides of the road, then proceed with caution if clear (stop, look and listen)
Skip the crossing and find another route
questions.explanation: When crossing a railroad and there are no warning devices, slow down, check both sides of the road then proceed with caution if clear (stop, look and listen).

questions.question: According to the source, what do warning or caution signs do?
options: Inform road users of traffic laws and regulations
Warn motorists of potentially hazardous conditions on or adjacent to the road
Give directions to the nearest hospital
questions.explanation: Signs used to warn motorists of potentially hazardous conditions on or adjacent to the road are called caution or warning signs.

questions.question: Where should you NOT overtake according to traffic rules?
options: At intersections, approaching a bridge, curve or crest, on solid lines, shoulders, railroad, hospital and school zones, and busy streets
questions.explanation: You should not overtake at intersections, when approaching a bridge, curve, or a crest, on solid yellow or white line, shoulder of the road, railroad, hospital and school zone, and busy streets.

questions.question: What does a single solid yellow line allow you to do?
options: Cross only when turning into a driveway
questions.explanation: In a single solid yellow line, you are allowed to cross only when turning into a driveway.

questions.question: What is the definition of defensive driving?
options: Driving as fast as possible to avoid danger
The practice of using driving techniques to minimize risk and help avoid road crash, demonstrating attitude, awareness and driving skills
Using only defensive weapons while driving
questions.explanation: Defensive driving is the practice of using driving techniques to minimize risk and help avoid road crash. It is an appropriate demonstration of attitude, awareness and driving skills.

questions.question: Which of the following is an act of road rage that a driver must avoid?
questions.explanation: Road rage acts include cutting off other motorists, rude gestures, tailgating, annoying blowing of horn, and obstructions.

questions.question: What is one of the tips to avoid road rage?
options: Put away your pride and forget about winning
questions.explanation: Tips to avoid road rage include: do not be aggressive and keep calm, maintain a safe distance, avoid retaliation, and put away your pride and forget about winning.

questions.question: What should you do if a motorist is driving against the flow of traffic toward you on a two-way road?
options: Insist on your right-of-way and hold your lane
Keep calm, do not insist on your right, make the proper signal and change your lane with care, and avoid eye-to-eye contact
Honk loudly and flash your lights aggressively
Stop in the middle of the road
questions.explanation: In the event of counterflow, keep calm and do not insist your right. Make the proper signal and change your lane with care. Avoid eye-to-eye contact with the oncoming motorists to reduce tension.

questions.question: If you are forced to ride off the road and cannot avoid hitting something, what should you look for to lessen the impact?
options: Something soft like bushes or something fixed like a fence, hitting it at an angle
questions.explanation: If you are forced to ride off the road and cannot avoid hitting other vehicles, properties, or pedestrians, look for something soft like bushes or something fixed like a fence, trying to glance off or hit it at an angle which lessens the impact.

questions.question: What should you do on an expressway regarding aggressive drivers?
questions.explanation: Expressway driving tip number 8 states: never provoke an aggressive driver.

questions.question: According to defensive driving tips, who should you give the right-of-way to?
options: Pedestrians such as PWDs, Senior Citizens, Children, Pregnant Women, and Road Workers
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to pedestrians such as PWDs, Senior Citizens, Children, Pregnant Women, Road Workers, and the likes.

questions.question: What does the Doctrine of Last Clear Chance state?
options: The faster driver is always at fault
A person who has the last chance of avoiding a road crash, despite the negligent acts of his opponent, is considered solely responsible
Both drivers share equal responsibility regardless of circumstances
The driver of the larger vehicle is always at fault
questions.explanation: The Doctrine of Last Clear Chance states that a person who has the last chance or opportunity of avoiding a road crash, despite the negligent acts of his opponent, is considered in law solely responsible for the consequences.

questions.question: What should you do when an elderly person crosses the pedestrian lane?
options: Be patient and allow them to cross
Proceed because you have the right-of-way
questions.explanation: When an elderly person crosses the pedestrian lane, be patient and allow them to cross.

questions.question: What should you do if you see a person in a wheelchair about to cross the street?
options: Stop and wait for the PWD to cross the street
Honk to alert them to hurry
Drive faster to pass before they cross
questions.explanation: If you see a person in a wheelchair who is about to cross the street, stop and wait for the PWD to cross the street.

questions.question: What should you do if you make a mistake while driving on the expressway?
options: Say or indicate "sorry" to the other driver
questions.explanation: Expressway driving tip number 16 states: say/indicate "sorry" if a mistake is committed.

questions.question: What is the overall attitude a driver should maintain on the expressway?
options: Be calm but aware and alert
questions.explanation: Expressway driving tip number 18 states: be calm but aware and alert.

questions.question: On a long drive, what should you do if you are tired or sleepy?
options: Park at an appropriate rest stop and take a few minutes nap
Open the windows and drive faster
Call someone to keep you awake
questions.explanation: On a long drive, if you are tired or sleepy, park at the appropriate rest stop and take a few minutes nap.

questions.question: What should you do when planning a long trip regarding rest?
options: Plan rest stops because regular stops help avoid mental and physical fatigue
Rest only when you reach the destination
questions.explanation: When planning a long trip, you need to plan rest stops because regular stops help avoid mental and physical fatigue.

questions.question: What does the expressway driving tip say about resting when tired?
options: Push through until the next exit
Rest in a safe place when tired or sleepy; don't take chances, do take a break
Only rest if you have a passenger to take over
questions.explanation: Expressway driving tip number 7 states: rest in a safe place when tired or sleepy. Don't take chances - do take a break.

questions.question: What could cause a driver to lose concentration while driving?
options: Listening to loud music, using mobile phone or gadget, watching videos, rubbernecking, and engaging in long conversations with passengers
questions.explanation: Reasons for losing concentration include listening to loud music, using mobile phone or gadget, watching videos, rubbernecking, and engaging in long conversations with passengers.

questions.question: What should you do if you are stopped by an enforcer even when you believe you did not violate any traffic rules?
options: Stop at the roadside and politely ask the reason why you were being stopped
questions.explanation: If stopped by an enforcer even when you believe you did not violate any traffic rules, stop at the roadside and politely ask the reason why you were being stopped.

questions.question: What should you do if the right-of-way is given to you on the expressway?
questions.explanation: Expressway driving tip number 17 states: say/indicate "thank you" if the right-of-way is given to you.

questions.question: What is proactive vehicle maintenance?
options: Repairing the vehicle only after it breaks down
A procedure where a driver undertakes due diligence in advance checking of the vehicle based on the service manual
Only changing the oil when the engine light comes on
questions.explanation: Proactive vehicle maintenance is a procedure where a driver of a vehicle undertakes due diligence in the advance checking of his/her vehicle based on the service manual. Proactive is the exact opposite of reactive maintenance.

questions.question: How does preventive maintenance differ from proactive maintenance?
options: Preventive is the replacement of identified parts as a result of inspection, while proactive is performing measures as stated in the service manual based on time or distance
Preventive is done before breakdown, proactive is done after breakdown
Preventive is for new vehicles only, proactive is for old vehicles
questions.explanation: Preventive is the replacement of identified parts as a result of inspection to avoid breakdowns while proactive is to perform measures as stated on the service manual of the vehicle.

questions.question: Before starting a vehicle with a manual clutch, what must you ensure?
options: The gear is in first position
The gear is in neutral position
questions.explanation: Manual clutch - be sure that the gear is in neutral position before starting.

questions.question: Before starting a vehicle with an automatic clutch, what must you ensure?
options: The shifting lever is at parking position
questions.explanation: Automatic clutch - make sure that the shifting lever is at parking position before starting.

questions.question: What adjustments should you make before starting to drive?
options: Adjust the seat and rearview mirror so that you can use it without having to lean forward or backward, and adjust side mirrors
Only adjust the steering wheel height
questions.explanation: Before starting to drive, adjust the seat and rearview mirror so that you can use it without having to lean forward or backward, adjust side mirrors, remove everything that blocks your view, and wear your seat belt.

questions.question: Within how many years of the manufacture date must brand new tires generally be used?
questions.explanation: Generally, brand new tires must be used within five (5) years of manufacture date. Do not buy expired brand-new tires.

questions.question: According to the FDM, when should you avoid checking tire pressure?
questions.explanation: Always check the load capacity of the tire and never check tire pressure when the tires are hot.

questions.question: What are the effects of underinflated or overinflated tire pressures?
options: Severely affects the vehicle's performance in terms of tire consumption, fuel consumption, braking performance, and driving at high speed
questions.explanation: Underinflated or overinflated tire pressures will severely affect the vehicle's performance in terms of tire consumption, fuel consumption, braking performance, and driving at a high speed.

questions.question: What are the usual causes of flat tires?
options: Improper tire inflation, overloading, and excessive use of tires (tread wear)
Only using the wrong brand of tire
questions.explanation: The usual causes of flat tires are improper tire inflation, overloading and excessive use of tires (tread wear).
