questions.question: What should you do to help reduce air pollution from your vehicle?
options: Drive faster to reduce emissions time
Do the regular motor vehicle check-up and do not overload
questions.explanation: To help reduce air pollution, do the regular motor vehicle check-up and do NOT overload.

questions.question: What can you contribute to ensure a clean air environment?
questions.explanation: To ensure a clean air environment, maintain an emission-compliant vehicle.

questions.question: What does black or gray smoke from a gasoline engine indicate?
questions.explanation: Black or gray smoke from a gasoline engine indicates smoke coming from incomplete fuel combustion, which may be caused by a clogged air filter, malfunctioning carburetor or injectors, improper ignition timing, blocked manifold, or oil leak in exhaust.

questions.question: What does blue smoke from a vehicle engine indicate?
options: The fuel is contaminated with water
questions.explanation: Blue smoke from both gasoline and diesel engines indicates engine oil burning, which may be caused by worn out piston rings, valves, or cylinders.

questions.question: What could be one of the possible causes of road crash if neglected?
options: Low level or leaking brake fluid
questions.explanation: One of the possible causes of road crash, if neglected, is low level or leaking brake fluid.

questions.question: What documents should a driver carry at all times when driving?
options: Driver's License, Certificate of Registration, and current Official Receipt (OR/CR)
questions.explanation: The documents a driver should carry at all times are Driver's License, Certificate of Registration, and current Official Receipt (OR/CR).

questions.question: Why should you check your vehicle thoroughly before making a long trip?
options: To prevent the inconvenience of vehicle breakdown
To test the vehicle's maximum speed
questions.explanation: You must check your vehicle thoroughly before making a long trip to prevent the inconvenience of vehicle breakdown.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?
options: Stop and wait for the green light
Slow down and proceed with caution
Speed up before the light changes
questions.explanation: Flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: What does a flashing red light mean?
options: Bring your vehicle to a stop and proceed only when it is safe
Slow down but do not stop
questions.explanation: Flashing red signal means bring your vehicle to a STOP and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a steady green traffic light mean?
options: You can proceed, provided you yield to pedestrians and traffic lawfully using the intersection
Speed up to clear the intersection
questions.explanation: Green signal means you can proceed, provided you yield to pedestrian and traffic lawfully using the intersection.

questions.question: What does a yellow or amber traffic light indicate?
options: Speed up to beat the red light
The red signal is about to appear
The intersection is clear for all directions
questions.explanation: Yellow / Amber signal indicates that the RED signal is about to appear.

questions.question: What is the recommended hand position on the steering wheel for good control?
questions.explanation: Hands grip on the steering wheel at a 9:3 or 10:2 position to have a good and full control of the steering wheel.

questions.question: At a roundabout or rotunda, who has the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: If you are about to enter a roundabout or rotunda, yield the right-of-way to vehicles already inside the roundabout.

questions.question: If two vehicles approach an intersection at approximately the same time, which vehicle has the right-of-way?
questions.explanation: When two vehicles approach or enter an intersection at approximately the same time, the driver of the vehicle on the left shall yield the right of way to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: When entering a highway from a private road or driveway, what must you do?
options: Enter immediately if no vehicles are visible
Yield the right-of-way to all vehicles approaching on such highway
Only yield to trucks and buses
questions.explanation: The driver of a vehicle entering a highway from a private road or drive shall yield the right-of-way to all vehicles approaching on such highway.

questions.question: When approaching a through highway or railroad crossing, what must you do when no hazard exists?
options: Come to a full stop always
The vehicle may be slowed down to five miles per hour instead of bringing it to a full stop
questions.explanation: When it is apparent that no hazard exists, the vehicle may be slowed down to five miles per hour instead of bringing it to a full stop before traversing any through highway or railroad crossing.

questions.question: What is the minimum speed limit on expressways?
questions.explanation: Expressway speed limits: minimum is 60 kph and maximum is 100 kph.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit on open country roads for passenger cars and motorcycles?
questions.explanation: On open country roads, with no blind corners not closely bordered by habitations, the prescribed speed for cars and motorcycles is 80 km per hour.

questions.question: What is the maximum permitted speed when driving within a school zone?
questions.explanation: Through crowded streets, approaching intersections at blind corners, passing school zones, passing other vehicles which are stationary, the speed limit is 20 km per hour. When driving within the school zone, the maximum permitted speed is 20 kph.

questions.question: What does a green arrow traffic light mean?
options: All vehicles may proceed in any direction
Vehicles turning in that direction shall proceed
Stop and wait for the full green light
questions.explanation: A green arrow traffic light means vehicles turning on that direction shall proceed.

questions.question: According to expressway rules, which lane is the innermost lane (Lane No. 1) used for?
options: Overtaking another vehicle within the allowed speed
questions.explanation: Lane No. 1 (innermost lane) or the lane nearest the Median Barrier shall be used only for overtaking another vehicle but within the allowed speed. Cargo trucks, buses, and slow-moving vehicles are NOT allowed in Lane No. 1 at all times.

questions.question: What does the law say about using mobile phones while driving?
options: Using mobile phones while driving is allowed if you are an experienced driver
Using mobile phones while driving is prohibited because it distracts your attention, pursuant to R.A. No. 10913 (Anti-Distracted Driving Act)
Using mobile phones is allowed on expressways only
Using mobile phones is allowed as long as you are not speeding
questions.explanation: Using mobile phones while driving is prohibited because it distracts your attention while driving, pursuant to R.A. No. 10913 (Anti-Distracted Driving Act).

questions.question: What is a Student-Driver's Permit (SP)?
options: An authority granted by the LTO to a person who desires to learn to operate a motor vehicle
A license to operate a motor vehicle for hire
A permit to drive without any supervision
A certificate that allows a person to teach others how to drive
questions.explanation: The SP is defined as 'an authority granted by the LTO to a person who desires to learn to operate a motor vehicle.'

questions.question: How long is a Student-Driver's Permit (SP) valid from the date of its issuance?
questions.explanation: The SP is valid for one (1) year from the date of its issuance.

questions.question: After one year from issuance, what can a Student-Driver's Permit still be used for?
options: To continue taking the practical driving course
To apply for a Non-Professional Driver's License if the practical driving course was completed within the one-year validity period
To operate a motor vehicle without a supervising driver
To renew the SP without any additional requirements
questions.explanation: After one year, the SP cannot be used for practical driving course but can be used to apply for NPDL if the practical driving course has been completed within the one year validity period.

questions.question: What is required after two years from the date of issuance of a Student-Driver's Permit?
options: The holder may simply renew the existing SP without any additional steps
The holder is required to acquire a new SP bearing the same SP number and undergo the required apprenticeship period
The holder must immediately apply for a Professional Driver's License
The holder must take a refresher course but keeps the same SP
questions.explanation: After two years from issuance, the holder is required to acquire a new SP bearing the same SP number and undergo the required apprenticeship period reckoned from the date of issuance of the new SP.

questions.question: Who must accompany the holder of a Student-Driver's Permit while operating a motor vehicle?
options: A duly licensed driver, accredited by LTO as a driving instructor, possessing the appropriate license codes
A family member with any type of driver's license
questions.explanation: The holder must be accompanied by a duly licensed driver, accredited by LTO as driving instructor, possessing the appropriate license codes.

questions.question: What is a Conductor's License (CL)?
options: A license to drive public utility vehicles
An authority granted by the LTO to a qualified person to assist the driver of a public utility vehicle in fare collection and/or ensuring safety of passengers and cargo
A permit to operate a bus
questions.explanation: A CL is defined as an authority granted by the LTO to a qualified person to assist the driver of a PUV in fare collection and/or ensuring the safety of passengers and cargo.

questions.question: A new Conductor's License (CL) is valid for how many years?
questions.explanation: A new CL is valid for five (5) years reckoned from the date of birth of the licensee.

questions.question: Under what condition is a CL holder entitled to a renewal valid for ten (10) years?
options: If the holder has completed an advanced training program
If the holder has not committed any violation during the five-year period preceding expiration
If the holder has paid an additional renewal fee
If the holder has been employed by a PUV operator for at least ten years
questions.explanation: A holder of CL who has not committed any violation/s during the five-year period preceding its expiration is entitled to renewal valid for ten years.

questions.question: What is required when renewing a Conductor's License more than two years after its expiry date?
options: Only payment of the basic renewal fee
The holder must take and pass the written examination and pay the corresponding penalty in addition to the basic fee
The holder must obtain a new Student-Driver's Permit first
The holder must present a new medical certificate only
questions.explanation: Renewal of CL after two (2) years from the expiry date shall require the holder to take and pass the written examination and pay the corresponding penalty.

questions.question: What is the minimum age for a Filipino to apply for a Student-Driver's Permit?
questions.explanation: Filipinos must be at least 16 years old to apply for a Student-Driver's Permit.

questions.question: What additional requirement is needed for Student-Driver's Permit applicants below 18 years of age?
options: Parental or guardian's consent with any valid government-issued ID with photo and signature
A certificate of good moral character
A recommendation letter from a driving school
questions.explanation: For applicants below 18 years of age, parental or guardian's consent with any valid government issued ID with photo and signature is required.

questions.question: What are the residency requirements for a foreigner applying for a Student-Driver's Permit?
options: At least 16 years old and been in the Philippines for at least six months
At least 18 years old, must have been in the Philippines for at least one month, and proof of stay for at least six months
At least 18 years old and must have been in the Philippines for at least one year
At least 17 years old and must present a valid working visa
questions.explanation: Foreigners must be at least 18 years old, must have been in the Philippines for at least one month, and provide proof of stay for at least six months.

questions.question: How many hours of Theoretical Driving Course (TDC) must an SP applicant complete?
questions.explanation: The applicant must have completed a 15-hour Theoretical Driving Course (TDC), which is auto-uploaded in the LTO Driver's License System.

questions.question: What is a Non-Professional Driver's License (NPDL)?
options: An authority to operate any type of motor vehicle for hire
An authority granted by the LTO to a person to operate a private motor vehicle
A license to operate heavy commercial vehicles
questions.explanation: NPDL is an authority granted by the LTO to a person to operate a private motor vehicle.

questions.question: What is a Professional Driver's License (PDL)?
options: An authority granted to any driver hired or paid for driving or operating a motor vehicle whether for private use or for hire to the public
A license only for government drivers
A license exclusively for bus drivers
A license that does not require any examination
questions.explanation: PDL is an authority granted to any driver hired or paid for driving or operating a motor vehicle whether for private use or for hire to the public.

questions.question: What does DL Code represent?
options: The collective code representing the vehicle category/ies that a licensed person is allowed to operate
The date the license was issued
The region where the license was issued
questions.explanation: DL Code refers to the collective code representing the vehicle category/ies that a licensed person is allowed to operate.

questions.question: What type of vehicles does DL Code A cover?
questions.explanation: DL Code A covers vehicle category L1, L2, L3 which refers to Motorcycle.

questions.question: What type of vehicles does DL Code A1 cover?
questions.explanation: DL Code A1 covers vehicle category L4, L5, L6, L7 which refers to Tricycle.

questions.question: Which DL Code corresponds to passenger cars (vehicle category M1)?
questions.explanation: DL Code B covers vehicle category M1 which refers to Passenger Car.

questions.question: What is the clutch code distinction for DL Code B1?
options: B1 is for automatic transmission only
B1 is for manual transmission (MT) for passenger van/jeepney (M2)
B1 is for both manual and automatic transmission
B1 is exclusively for electric vehicles
questions.explanation: DL Code B1 covers vehicle category M2 with Manual Transmission (MT) for passenger van/jeepney.

questions.question: What type of vehicles does DL Code C cover?
questions.explanation: DL Code C covers vehicle categories N2, N3 which refers to Heavy Commercial vehicles.

questions.question: Which DL Code corresponds to passenger buses?
questions.explanation: DL Code D covers vehicle category M3 which refers to Passenger Bus.

questions.question: What vehicle categories does DL Code BE cover?
options: N1 and N2 light commercial vehicles
O1 and O2 light articulated vehicles
questions.explanation: DL Code BE covers vehicle categories O1, O2 which refers to Light Articulated vehicles.

questions.question: Which statement is true regarding Manual Transmission (MT) and Automatic Transmission (AT) clutch codes?
options: Holders of DL with AT Clutch Code are allowed to operate vehicles with MT
Holders of DL with MT Clutch Code are allowed to operate vehicles with AT
Both MT and AT holders can operate any type of transmission
Neither MT nor AT holders can operate the other type
questions.explanation: Holders of DL with MT Clutch Code are allowed to operate vehicles with AT. Holders of DL with AT Clutch Code are NOT allowed to operate vehicles with MT.

questions.question: For new driver's license applicants, which DL Codes are they allowed to apply for under NPDL?
options: A, A1, B, B1, and B2, or any combination thereof
All DL Codes including C, D, and CE
questions.explanation: For new DL, applicants are only allowed to apply for NPDL under DL Codes A, A1, B, B1 and B2, or combination thereof.

questions.question: A new Driver's License is valid for how many years?
questions.explanation: A new DL is valid for five (5) years reckoned from the date of birth of the licensee, unless sooner revoked or suspended.

questions.question: Under what condition is a DL holder entitled to a renewal valid for ten (10) years?
options: If the holder has completed a special training course
If the holder has not committed any violation during the five-year period preceding expiration
If the holder has paid double the renewal fee
If the holder is at least 60 years old
questions.explanation: A DL holder who has not committed any violation/s during the five-year period preceding its expiration is entitled to a renewal valid for ten years.

questions.question: What is the Driving Enhancement Program (DEP)?
options: An advanced driving course for racing
An updated road safety seminar designed by LTO for DL holders required prior to renewal of the initial five-year license
A medical examination required for all drivers
questions.explanation: DEP is an updated road safety seminar designed by LTO for DL holders, required prior to renewal of the initial five-year license.

questions.question: What is the maximum design speed of an L1 category vehicle?
questions.explanation: L1 is a two-wheeled vehicle with a maximum design speed not exceeding 50 kph.

questions.question: What type of vehicle is described as having four wheels, an unladen mass not more than 350 kg, and a maximum design speed not more than 45 kph?
questions.explanation: L6 is a vehicle with four wheels whose unladen mass is not more than 350 kg and whose maximum design speed is not more than 45 kph.

questions.question: What is the maximum gross vehicle weight of an N1 category vehicle?
questions.explanation: N1 vehicles are used for the carriage of goods and have a maximum gross vehicle weight not exceeding 3500 kg.

questions.question: According to the manual, a driver's license is considered a:
questions.explanation: The manual explicitly states: 'DRIVER'S LICENSE IS A PRIVILEGE, NOT A RIGHT'.

questions.question: What does Medical Condition Code 1 indicate on a driver's license?
questions.explanation: Condition Code 1 means the licensee must drive only with corrective lenses and is certified to be out of the 20/40 vision.

questions.question: What does Medical Condition Code 2 indicate on a driver's license?
options: Drive only with special equipment for upper limbs and/or lower limbs
questions.explanation: Condition Code 2 means drive only with special equipment for upper limbs and/or lower limbs, for licensees with impairment at the upper limb and/or lower limb.

questions.question: What does Medical Condition Code 4 indicate on a driver's license?
options: Drive only with special equipment for limbs
questions.explanation: Condition Code 4 means drive only during daylight and includes partially or totally blind in one eye.

questions.question: What does Medical Condition Code 5 indicate?
questions.explanation: Condition Code 5 means drive only with hearing aid, indicated for a licensee with impaired hearing.

questions.question: What restriction applies to drivers with medical condition codes 2, 3, 4, or 5?
options: They are not allowed to operate For-Hire/Public Utility Vehicles or Commercial Vehicles unless expressly allowed in writing by a qualified medical specialist
They must renew their license every year
questions.explanation: Drivers with driving conditions 2, 3, 4, or 5 are not allowed to operate For-Hire/PUV or Commercial Vehicles, unless expressly allowed in writing by a qualified medical specialist.

questions.question: How long is a Medical Certificate valid from the date of issuance?
questions.explanation: A Medical Certificate is valid for a period of sixty (60) days from the date of issuance.

questions.question: What is the minimum age to apply for a Non-Professional Driver's License (NPDL)?
questions.explanation: Applicants for NPDL must be at least 17 years old. Parental or guardian's consent is required if the applicant is 17 years old.

questions.question: What is the literacy requirement for all LTO license and permit applicants?
options: Must be able to read and write in Filipino, English, or any major dialect
Must be able to speak English fluently
Must have completed at least high school
questions.explanation: All applicants must be able to read and write in Filipino, English or any major dialect.

questions.question: What is the minimum age to apply for a Conductor's License?
questions.explanation: The minimum age for a Conductor's License is at least 18 years old.

questions.question: For how long must an applicant hold a Student-Driver's Permit before applying for a Non-Professional Driver's License?
questions.explanation: The applicant must be an SP holder for at least one (1) month before applying for a new DL.

questions.question: What practical training must be completed before applying for a new Driver's License?
options: A seminar on road courtesy only
The practical driving course (PDC) from an LTO accredited instructor, LTO Driver's Education Center, or LTO accredited Driving School/TESDA Training Center
questions.explanation: The applicant must have attended and passed the PDC from LTO accredited instructor, LTO Driver's Education Center or LTO accredited Driving School/TESDA Training Center.

questions.question: What examination must a new Driver's License applicant pass?
options: Both the Automated Theoretical Examination and the Practical Driving Test
questions.explanation: New DL applicants must pass both the Automated Theoretical Examination and the Practical Driving Test.

questions.question: For new Driver's License applicants, what requirement is common to all DL code categories A, A1, B, B1, and B2?
options: Must have at least one year driving experience
Must have a valid Student-Driver's Permit
questions.explanation: A valid SP is a requirement for all new DL applicants under codes A, A1, B, B1, B2.

questions.question: What is the minimum age for a foreigner applying for a Non-Professional Driver's License?
questions.explanation: For foreigners applying for NPDL, the minimum age is at least 18 years old.

questions.question: What is the physical and mental requirement for a Conductor's License applicant?
options: Must pass a physical fitness test only
Must be physically and mentally fit to work and have no contagious disease
Must be at least 5 feet tall
questions.explanation: CL applicants must be physically and mentally fit to work and have no contagious disease.

questions.question: When can a Driver's License be renewed before its expiry date?
options: On or before but not earlier than sixty (60) days from the expiry date
Only on the exact expiry date
Up to one week after expiry
Any time within six months before expiry
questions.explanation: All licenses may be applied for renewal on or before but not earlier than sixty (60) days from the expiry date.

questions.question: Under what condition may a Driver's License be renewed one year in advance?
options: If the licensee is a senior citizen
Upon presentation of a valid transportation ticket as proof of imminent travel
If the licensee has a perfect driving record
If the licensee pays double the renewal fee
questions.explanation: A DL may be renewed one (1) year in advance upon presentation of a valid transportation ticket as proof of imminent travel.

questions.question: What is required when renewing a Driver's License more than two years after its expiry date?
options: Only payment of the basic fee and penalty
The holder must take and pass the theoretical and practical examination and pay the corresponding penalty in addition to the basic fee
The holder must obtain a new Student-Driver's Permit
The holder can still renew without any additional requirements
questions.explanation: Renewal of DL after two years from the expiry date shall require the holder to take and pass the theoretical and practical examination and pay the corresponding penalty.

questions.question: After how many calendar days may a failed practical driving test applicant re-apply?
questions.explanation: Failed applicants may re-apply after seven (7) calendar days.

questions.question: Where must the Practical Driving Test be conducted?
options: Within the LTO authorized test route only
questions.explanation: The Practical Driving Test shall be done within the LTO authorized test route. Any test conducted outside the designated test route shall be declared null and void.

questions.question: A valid Foreign Driver's License may be converted into a Philippine DL limited to which DL Codes?
options: All DL codes including C, D, and CE
A, A1, B, B1, and/or B2 only
questions.explanation: Valid FDL may be converted into Philippine DL but limited to DL Code A, A1, B, B1 and/or B2 only.

questions.question: For how many days is a bona fide tourist with a valid Foreign Driver's License allowed to operate motor vehicles in the Philippines?
options: No more than one hundred twenty (120) days
questions.explanation: A bona fide tourist with valid FDL is allowed to operate motor vehicles for no more than ninety (90) days of their stay in the Philippines.

questions.question: How many days of valid visa must a foreign national have upon arrival to convert a Foreign Driver's License to a Philippine DL?
questions.explanation: Foreign nationals must have a valid visa for at least 120 days upon the date of arrival.

questions.question: What is the minimum experience requirement for applying for Additional DL Code C?
options: Must be a holder of PDL Code B1 for at least two years
Must be a holder of PDL Code B2 for at least four years
Must be a holder of NPDL Code B for at least three years
Must be a holder of any DL for at least five years
questions.explanation: For Additional DL Code C, the applicant must be a holder of PDL Code B2 for at least four (4) years and must have training from LTO accredited TESDA Training Center for NC III or PDC from Driving School.

questions.question: What is the minimum experience requirement for applying for Additional DL Code D?
options: Must be a holder of PDL Code B2 for at least four years
Must be a holder of PDL Code B1 for at least four years
Must be a holder of PDL Code B for at least three years
Must be a holder of PDL Code C for at least two years
questions.explanation: For Additional DL Code D, the applicant must be a holder of PDL Code B1 for at least four (4) years and must have equivalent training.

questions.question: What is the experience requirement for applying for Additional DL Code CE?
options: Holder of C or D for at least six months
Holder of B2 for at least four years
Holder of B1 for at least three years
Holder of B for at least one year
questions.explanation: For Additional DL Code CE, the applicant must be a holder of C or D for at least six (6) months and must have equivalent training from LTO Accredited TESDA NC III Training Center or PDC.

questions.question: What must a DL holder with an Automatic Transmission (AT) Clutch Code do to operate a manual transmission vehicle?
options: Nothing, AT holders can already operate MT vehicles
Take and pass the practical driving test
Apply for a new Student-Driver's Permit
questions.explanation: A DL holder with AT Clutch Code who intends to operate manual transmission must take and pass the practical driving test.

questions.question: For holders of DL Codes A or A1 with an NPDL, how long must they hold the NPDL before applying for a PDL?
questions.explanation: Holders of DL Codes A, A1 who are at least eighteen years old may apply for PDL after being a holder for six (6) months of NPDL with the same DL Codes.

questions.question: For holders of DL Codes B, B1, or B2 with an NPDL, how long must they hold the NPDL before applying for a PDL?
questions.explanation: Holders of DL Codes B, B1, B2 who are at least eighteen years old may apply for PDL after being a holder for one (1) year of NPDL with the same DL Codes.

questions.question: For dropping a DL classification, what qualifications or documentary requirements are needed other than the APL form?
options: No other qualifications or documentary requirements are required, provided the DL is valid
questions.explanation: For dropping of DL Classification, other than APL, provided that such DL is valid, no other qualifications or documentary requirements are required.

questions.question: Can Filipinos working or living abroad renew their Driver's License?
options: No, they must return to the Philippines in person
Yes, they may renew their DL online or through their authorized representative upon presentation of necessary documents
Only if they have a valid foreign driver's license
Only within 30 days of the expiry date
questions.explanation: Filipinos working/living abroad may renew their DL on-line or through their authorized representative upon presentation of necessary documents.

questions.question: What is required for DL renewal at the initial five-year mark?
options: Obtaining a new medical certificate only
questions.explanation: The applicant must have completed the Driving Enhancement Program (DEP) prior to initial renewal of the five (5) year DL.

questions.question: For Additional DL Code BE, what is the alternative to holding B, B1, or B2 for at least three years?
options: Holder of A for five years
Holder of any DL for ten years
questions.explanation: For Additional DL Code BE, the applicant must be a holder of B, B1 or B2 for at least three years, or holder of CE.

questions.question: What training institution is responsible for certifying fire truck drivers?
questions.explanation: Firetruck drivers must have a Certificate of Training from the National Fire Training Institute.

questions.question: What is required for Conversion of a Foreign Driver's License if the foreign license is invalid?
options: Only payment of the conversion fee
The applicant must pass the theoretical examination and practical driving test
The applicant must obtain a new SP first
questions.explanation: In case of invalid foreign DL, the applicant must pass the theoretical examination and practical driving test.

questions.question: What is the total fee for a new Student-Driver's Permit?
questions.explanation: The new SP fee totals Php 317.63, composed of Application Fee (100.00), Computer Fee (67.63), and Permit Fee (150.00).

questions.question: What is the total fee for a new Conductor's License or Driver's License?
questions.explanation: The new DL/CL fee totals Php 820.26, composed of Application Fee (100.00), Computer Fee (67.63), License Fee (585.00), and Computer Fee (67.63).

questions.question: What is the penalty fee for a license not renewed within 1 day to 2 years after expiry?
questions.explanation: The penalty fee for 1 day to 2 years late renewal is Php 75.00.

questions.question: What is the penalty fee for a license not renewed for more than 2 years (re-examination required)?
questions.explanation: For licenses expired more than two (2) years requiring re-examination, the penalty is Php 225.00.

questions.question: What is the application fee for any LTO license or permit transaction?
questions.explanation: The application fee for both Student-Driver's Permit and Conductor's/Driver's License is Php 100.00.

questions.question: What is the total fee for the renewal of a delinquent Conductor's or Driver's License?
questions.explanation: The renewal of delinquent license totals Php 1,045.26, composed of Application Fee (100.00), Computer Fee (67.63), License Fee (585.00), Computer Fee (67.63), and Penalty (225.00).

questions.question: What is the replacement fee for a lost or mutilated license?
questions.explanation: The replacement fee for a lost or mutilated license is Php 225.00.

questions.question: What is the computer fee for each license transaction?
questions.explanation: The computer fee for each transaction is Php 67.63.

questions.question: What is the penalty fee for a license not renewed for more than 1 year to 2 years after expiry?
questions.explanation: The penalty fee for more than 1 year to 2 years late renewal is Php 150.00.

questions.question: What is the total fee for an Application for Additional Restriction Code on a valid license that is also due for renewal?
questions.explanation: The total fee for Additional Restriction Code on a valid license due for renewal is Php 920.26, plus Php 100.00 per RC.

questions.question: According to the Driver's Education course content, what are the three main course modules for driving schools?
options: Motorcycle, Light Vehicle, and Heavy Vehicle
questions.explanation: The course content of driving schools is divided into three modules: Motorcycle (A, A1), Light Vehicle (B, B1, B2, BE), and Heavy Vehicle (C, CE, D).

questions.question: Which DL codes are covered by the Motorcycle module of the driving school course?
questions.explanation: The Motorcycle module covers DL codes A and A1.

questions.question: Which DL codes are covered by the Heavy Vehicle module of the driving school course?
questions.explanation: The Heavy Vehicle module covers DL codes C, CE, and D.

questions.question: What is the first major section (Part I) of every driving school module?
questions.explanation: Part I of each module (Motorcycle, Light Vehicle, Heavy Vehicle) is the Theoretical Driving Course.

questions.question: In the Motorcycle Theoretical Driving Course, which government agency mandates are covered under Introduction to Driving?
options: LTO, LTFRB, MMDA, HPG, and other law enforcement agencies
questions.explanation: The Introduction to Driving covers the organization and mandate of LTO, LTFRB, MMDA, HPG and other law enforcement agencies.

questions.question: What does TLSL stand for in the driving school course content?
options: Think, Look, Signal, and Look again
questions.explanation: TLSL stands for 'think, look, signal and look again' as referenced in the motorcycle turning procedure.

questions.question: What does SIPDE stand for in the Defensive Driving section?
options: Scanning process and leaving yourself an out
questions.explanation: SIPDE is associated with driver perception and awareness, specifically the scanning process and leaving yourself an out.

questions.question: Which road safety law is covered in the Motorcycle module but NOT in the Light Vehicle module?
options: R.A. No. 10586 - Anti-Drunk and Drugged Driving Act
R.A. No. 10054 - Motorcycle Helmet Act of 2009
R.A. No. 4136 - Land Transportation and Traffic Code
questions.explanation: R.A. No. 10054 (Motorcycle Helmet Act of 2009), R.A. No. 10666, R.A. No. 11235 are listed in the Motorcycle module but not in the Light Vehicle module.

questions.question: Which road safety law is included in the Light Vehicle module but NOT in the Motorcycle module?
options: R.A. No. 4136 - Land Transportation and Traffic Code
R.A. No. 10586 - Anti-Drunk and Drugged Driving Act
R.A. No. 8750 - Seat Belts Use Act of 1999
questions.explanation: R.A. No. 8750 (Seat Belts Use Act of 1999), R.A. No. 8749, R.A. No. 8794, R.A. No. 10916, and R.A. No. 11229 are listed in the Light Vehicle module but not in the Motorcycle module.

questions.question: In the Light Vehicle module, what are the two recommended steering wheel hand positions?
questions.explanation: The two recommended hand positions for handling the steering wheel are 9-and-3 and 10-and-2.

questions.question: In the Motorcycle module, how far ahead should a rider look according to the eye clearance and distance test?
questions.explanation: The Motorcycle module states to look 10 to 15 seconds ahead as part of the eye clearance and distance test.

questions.question: What is the pre-start routine for light vehicles before driving?
options: Closing and locking doors, proper sitting position, adjustment of steering wheel, adjustment of mirrors, and wearing of seat belt
Checking tire pressure and fuel level only
questions.explanation: The pre-start routine for light vehicles includes closing and locking doors, proper sitting position, adjustment of steering wheel, adjustment of mirrors, and wearing of seat belt.

questions.question: What does BLOWBAGA refer to in the Heavy Vehicle module's walk around check?
options: A systematic inspection procedure for checking the vehicle exterior
A driving technique for heavy vehicles
questions.explanation: The Heavy Vehicle module refers to a systematic inspection of the vehicle using BLOWBAGA during the walk around check (exterior).

questions.question: What is the following distance rule for light vehicles mentioned in the defensive driving section?
questions.explanation: The Light Vehicle defensive driving section mentions the two (2) or three (3) second rule for speed management limits.

questions.question: What is the following distance rule for heavy vehicles mentioned in the defensive driving section?
questions.explanation: The Heavy Vehicle defensive driving section mentions the six (6) second rule for speed management limits.

questions.question: In all driving course modules, what parking scenarios must the driver demonstrate?
options: Parking on level ground, downhill and uphill (with curb and without curb)
questions.explanation: All Practical Driving Courses require parking on level ground, downhill and uphill (with curb and without curb).

questions.question: What are the four basic types of retarders listed in the Heavy Vehicle module?
questions.explanation: The Heavy Vehicle module lists the basic types of retarders as Exhaust, Engine, Hydraulic, and Electric.

questions.question: In the Motorcycle module, what protective gear is listed under Pre-Driving Orientation accessories?
options: Jacket, pants, shoes, gloves, pads, and goggles
questions.explanation: The protection gears listed include jacket, pants, shoes, gloves, pads, and goggles, in addition to the helmet.

questions.question: In the Heavy Vehicle module, what documents must a For-Hire driver carry, in addition to the OR/CR and Driver's License?
options: Certificate of Public Convenience, Manifest, Trip Report or Dispatch Report, Necessary Permit, and Insurance Policy
Only the Driver's License and OR/CR
questions.explanation: Heavy vehicle drivers must carry: OR/CR, Driver's License, Certificate of Public Convenience, Manifest, Trip Report or Dispatch Report, Necessary Permit, and Insurance Policy.

questions.question: What emergency situations are covered in the Handling Emergencies section of all three course modules?
options: Tire blowout, overheat, loss of brake, tire skid, fire, and roll over
Only flat tire and engine failure
questions.explanation: All three modules cover tire blowout, overheat, loss of brake (brake fade and sticking brake), tire skid, fire, and roll over.

questions.question: In all three driving course modules, what are the common factors affecting concentration under Defensive Driving?
questions.explanation: Factors affecting concentration include man-made (distracted driving) and physiological factors, as listed in all three modules.

questions.question: In the Heavy Vehicle module's Cargo Handling section, what procedures are covered?
options: Cargo and goods handling, strapping/covering/restraining of cargo, dealing with hazardous materials, and emergency procedures
questions.explanation: Cargo Handling (Truck) covers: cargo and goods handling, strapping/covering/restraining of cargo, dealing with hazardous materials, and emergency procedures.

questions.question: What documents must a motorcycle/tricycle driver carry according to the Motorcycle module?
options: Updated OR/CR, Driver's License, and Motorized Tricycle Operator's Permit (MTOP)
questions.explanation: The Motorcycle module lists: Updated Official Receipt and Certificate of Registration, Driver's License, and Motorized Tricycle Operator's Permit.

questions.question: What does the letter B stand for in the BLOWBAGETS pre-drive vehicle inspection checklist?
questions.explanation: The BLOWBAGETS checklist begins with Battery, which includes limiting short rides, keeping batteries tightly fastened, turning off all lights before getting off, controlling corrosion, and not using gadgets when the engine is off.

questions.question: Before starting the engine of a vehicle with a manual clutch, where must the gear be positioned?
options: Any gear with the clutch depressed
questions.explanation: The FDM states that for a manual clutch, you must be sure that the gear is in neutral position before starting.

questions.question: Before starting the engine of a vehicle with an automatic clutch, where must the shifting lever be positioned?
questions.explanation: For an automatic clutch, the FDM instructs the driver to make sure that the shifting lever is at parking position before starting.

questions.question: What does the letter L stand for in the BLOWBAGETS pre-drive vehicle inspection checklist?
questions.explanation: The L in BLOWBAGETS stands for Light; drivers are advised to always clean the lens, switch lights on before sunset, and keep windshield and mirrors clean.

questions.question: What does the letter O stand for in the BLOWBAGETS pre-drive vehicle inspection checklist?
questions.explanation: The O in BLOWBAGETS stands for Oil; drivers should check the engine oil level regularly, change oil at regular intervals, and check for oil leaks.

questions.question: What does the letter W stand for in the BLOWBAGETS pre-drive vehicle inspection checklist?
questions.explanation: The W in BLOWBAGETS stands for Water (Coolant); drivers should check the water level regularly, avoid overfilling the reservoir, and check upper and lower hoses.

questions.question: What does the letter T stand for in the BLOWBAGETS pre-drive vehicle inspection checklist?
questions.explanation: The T in BLOWBAGETS stands for Tires; drivers should always check tire pressure before leaving or every scheduled stop.

questions.question: What should a driver do with the seatbelt before starting to drive?
options: Wear the seatbelt and advise passengers to do the same
Only wear the seatbelt if driving on the expressway
Fasten the seatbelt after reaching 40 kph
Only the driver needs to wear the seatbelt
questions.explanation: The FDM instructs drivers to make sure to wear your seat belt and advise passengers to do the same before starting to drive.

questions.question: Aside from the BLOWBAGETS checklist, which of the following must a motorcycle rider additionally check before driving?
options: Accelerator and brake cable, accelerator throttle, and drive chain or belt
Sidecar attachment bolts and passenger foot pegs
Fuel octane rating and engine compression
Kickstand spring tension and handlebar grip condition
questions.explanation: For motorcycle riders, the FDM states that aside from BLOWBAGETS, they should check the accelerator and brake cable, accelerator throttle, and drive chain or belt.

questions.question: Before driving, what should be removed to ensure a clear view of the road?
options: Only the sunshade on the windshield
questions.explanation: The FDM instructs drivers to remove everything that blocks your view as part of the pre-driving preparations.

questions.question: According to the BLOWBAGETS checklist, when should you switch your vehicle lights ON?
options: Only when it is completely dark
questions.explanation: The FDM explicitly states to make sure to switch the lights ON before sunset as part of the BLOWBAGETS checklist.

questions.question: If possible, at what distance should you switch to low beam lights when approaching a car in front of you?
questions.explanation: The FDM advises switching to low beam lights if you are within 200 meters of the car in front of you.

questions.question: What should you do with cabin lights when the engine is off?
options: Only turn them off if the battery is old
questions.explanation: The FDM states to switch OFF cabin lights when the engine is off as part of the BLOWBAGETS light checklist.

questions.question: What should be regularly maintained on vehicle lights according to the BLOWBAGETS checklist?
questions.explanation: The FDM advises to always clean lens as part of the light maintenance in the BLOWBAGETS checklist.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light on a traffic signal mean?
options: Slow down and proceed with caution
Stop and wait for the green light
Speed up before the light turns red
Stop only if pedestrians are present
questions.explanation: The FDM states that a flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic signal mean?
options: Bring the vehicle to a stop and proceed only when it is safe
Stop completely and wait for a green signal no matter what
questions.explanation: The FDM states that a flashing red signal means bring your vehicle to a STOP and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a steady red traffic signal mean?
options: Bring the vehicle to a stop at the marked line
Slow down and prepare to stop
Proceed if the intersection is clear
Yield to vehicles on the right
questions.explanation: The FDM states that a red signal means you must bring your vehicle to a STOP at a marked line.

questions.question: What does a steady green traffic signal indicate?
options: Proceed, provided you yield to pedestrians and traffic lawfully using the intersection
Speed up to clear the intersection quickly
Stop and wait for a green arrow
questions.explanation: The FDM states that a green signal means you can proceed, provided you yield to pedestrian and traffic lawfully using the intersection.

questions.question: What does a yellow or amber traffic signal indicate?
options: The red signal is about to appear
The green signal is about to appear
The intersection is clear of pedestrians
questions.explanation: The FDM states that a yellow/amber signal indicates that the RED signal is about to appear.

questions.question: What does the BLOWBAGETS checklist advise about excessive vehicle lights?
options: Use as many auxiliary lights as possible
Only use excessive lights on highways
Excessive lights are recommended in rural areas
questions.explanation: The FDM explicitly states to avoid using excessive lights in the BLOWBAGETS checklist under the Lights category.

questions.question: What should be checked on the brake master cylinder according to the BLOWBAGETS checklist?
options: Check the color of the paint
Check the temperature of the cylinder
questions.explanation: The FDM instructs drivers to check for oil leaks on the brake master cylinder as part of the BLOWBAGETS brakes checklist.

questions.question: After repairing the brakes, what should the driver do?
options: Drive the vehicle and apply intermittent brake within a block
Apply the parking brake firmly and leave it engaged
questions.explanation: The FDM states that after repair, the driver should drive the vehicle and apply intermittent brake within a block.

questions.question: What characteristics of the brake fluid reservoir should be checked under BLOWBAGETS?
questions.explanation: The FDM specifies to check the fluid reservoir for color and odor as part of the BLOWBAGETS brakes checklist.

questions.question: What is the braking distance of a vehicle running at 100 kph under ideal conditions when applying a full brake?
questions.explanation: The FDM states that a vehicle running at 100 kph in an ideal condition can travel 60 meters when applying a full brake.

questions.question: What is the perception distance of a vehicle running at 100 kph?
questions.explanation: The FDM states that a vehicle running at 100 kph has a perception distance of 20 meters.

questions.question: What is the total stopping distance of a vehicle running at 100 kph on a full brake?
questions.explanation: The FDM states that a vehicle running at 100 kph has a total stopping distance of 80 meters on a full brake.

questions.question: What is the Two or Three Second Rule primarily a guide to?
questions.explanation: The FDM states the two or three second rule is not a guide to safe distance but more of a guide to reaction time.

questions.question: What should be checked on the brake caliper or piston according to the BLOWBAGETS checklist?
options: Check for rust on the exterior only
questions.explanation: The FDM instructs drivers to check for oil leaks on the caliper or piston as part of the BLOWBAGETS brakes checklist.

questions.question: Why should rotors and brake pads be regularly washed according to BLOWBAGETS?
options: To improve their color and appearance
questions.explanation: The FDM states to regularly wash the rotors and pads to remove residuals or dusts as part of the BLOWBAGETS brakes checklist.

questions.question: Which part of the BLOWBAGETS checklist includes checking the parking brake?
questions.explanation: The parking brake is checked under the Accessories category in BLOWBAGETS, alongside the horn, spare tire, early warning device, AC components, seatbelt, etc.

questions.question: In the absence of a tire pressure chart, what is the ideal maximum tire pressure when the tires are cold?
questions.explanation: The FDM states that in the absence of a chart usually situated near the driver seat, the ideal maximum tire pressure when cold is minus 4 psi.

questions.question: What are common tire problems usually due to according to the BLOWBAGETS checklist?
options: Using the wrong brand of tires
questions.explanation: The FDM states that the common tire problems are due to toe-in or toe-out, which may be observed after a long trip.

questions.question: At what angle should tires be rotated whenever the vehicle has been parked to prevent cracks on sidewalls?
questions.explanation: The FDM states to rotate the tires at 45 degrees whenever the vehicle has been parked to prevent cracks on sidewalls.

questions.question: What vehicle components greatly affect the wear and tear of tires according to BLOWBAGETS?
options: Worn out kingpins and control arms
Worn out spark plugs and ignition coils
questions.explanation: The FDM states that worn out kingpins and control arms greatly affect the wear and tear of tire.

questions.question: What can underinflated or overinflated tire pressures severely affect?
options: Tire consumption, fuel consumption, braking performance, and driving at high speed
questions.explanation: The FDM states that underinflated or overinflated tire pressures will severely affect the vehicle's performance in terms of tire consumption, fuel consumption, braking performance and driving at a high speed.

questions.question: Within how many years of the manufacture date must brand new tires generally be used?
questions.explanation: The FDM states generally, brand new tires must be used within five (5) years of manufacture date.

questions.question: When should you never check tire pressure?
questions.explanation: The FDM instructs to never check tire pressure when the tires are hot.

questions.question: Which tires on a motorcycle usually wear first?
options: Both wear at the same rate
questions.explanation: The FDM states that rear tires of motorcycles usually wear first.

questions.question: What should you do before upgrading your vehicle's tire sizes?
options: Simply buy the largest available size
questions.explanation: The FDM advises to stick to the tire specification of the motor vehicle and consult tire professionals before upgrading your tire sizes.

questions.question: What portable item should you always bring if possible for tire emergencies?
questions.explanation: The FDM advises to never drive with a flat tire, and if possible, always bring a portable air compressor.

questions.question: What is the standard equipment for reversing or backing up a vehicle?
questions.explanation: The FDM states that the rearview mirror is the standard equipment for reversing (also known as backing up).

questions.question: What mirrors should a driver adjust before starting to drive?
options: Both the rearview mirror and side mirrors
questions.explanation: The FDM instructs drivers to adjust the seat and rearview mirror so that you can use it without having to lean forward or backward, and to adjust side mirrors.

questions.question: What must a motorcycle rider check and adjust before starting to drive?
questions.explanation: The FDM instructs motorcycle riders to check and adjust the side mirrors before starting to drive.

questions.question: What should be kept clean along with windshield according to the BLOWBAGETS light checklist?
questions.explanation: The FDM instructs to keep windshield and mirrors clean as part of the BLOWBAGETS light checklist.

questions.question: Under which BLOWBAGETS category are side and rearview mirrors checked?
questions.explanation: Side and rearview mirrors are checked under the Accessories category in BLOWBAGETS, alongside body scratches, doors, windows, wipers, and cluster instruments.

questions.question: Which of the following is checked under the Accessories category in BLOWBAGETS?
questions.explanation: The early warning device is checked under Accessories in BLOWBAGETS, along with horn, spare tire, AC components, seatbelt, and parking brake.

questions.question: Which safety device is checked under the Accessories category in the BLOWBAGETS checklist?
questions.explanation: The seatbelt is checked under the Accessories category in BLOWBAGETS, along with horn, spare tire, early warning device, AC components, and parking brake.

questions.question: What modern safety aids do modern motor vehicles have for reversing?
options: Built-in technical aids or sensors like backup cameras
questions.explanation: The FDM states that modern motor vehicles have built-in technical aids or sensors like backup cameras for reversing.

questions.question: What happens if the side stand of a modern motorcycle is not properly placed?
options: The motorcycle will not move and the engine will go OFF
questions.explanation: The FDM states that modern motorcycles will not move, and the engine will go OFF if the side stand is not properly placed.

questions.question: When should you switch on the hazard warning light on an expressway?
options: Whenever driving below the minimum speed
During heavy rain at all times
questions.explanation: The FDM instructs drivers to switch on hazard warning light only when stopping for emergencies on the expressway.

questions.question: What is required to be worn at all times by motorcycle riders on the expressway?
questions.explanation: The FDM states that for motorcycles on the expressway, helmets must be worn at all times.

questions.question: What should a driver do with the doors before starting to drive?
options: Leave the doors unlocked for quick exit
Open the windows before locking doors
questions.explanation: The FDM instructs drivers to lock all doors as part of the pre-driving procedures before starting to drive.

questions.question: Why should a motorcycle rider never condemn starting or moving sensors on a modern motorcycle?
options: They will keep the rider safe
questions.explanation: The FDM advises motorcycle riders to never condemn starting or moving sensors, stating these will keep you safe.

questions.question: What is the main problem when reversing a vehicle that leads to road crashes?
questions.explanation: The FDM states that the main problem when reversing is poor visibility resulting to road crashes.

questions.question: What safety equipment can be installed to prevent reversing-related road crashes?
questions.explanation: The FDM states that to prevent reversing-related road crashes, one can install safety equipment including cameras and sensors.

questions.question: Which of the following is a required vehicle document according to the FDM?
questions.explanation: The FDM lists Certificate of Registration, New Official Receipt, Driver's License, and Certificate of Public Convenience/Franchise as required documents.

questions.question: Which document must a driver carry in addition to a Driver's License and Certificate of Registration?
questions.explanation: The FDM lists the New Official Receipt as one of the required documents along with the Certificate of Registration and Driver's License.

questions.question: What is the minimum engine displacement for motorcycles allowed on the expressway?
questions.explanation: The FDM states that motorcycles below 400 cc are not allowed to enter the expressway, meaning 400 cc and above is the minimum.

questions.question: Which of the following vehicles is NOT allowed on the expressway at any time?
options: Freight vehicles with under 1.5 ton cargo
questions.explanation: The FDM lists tricycles, all kinds of scooters, and bicycles among vehicles not allowed on the expressway at any time, alongside motorcycles below 400 cc.

questions.question: Which vehicle condition makes a vehicle NOT roadworthy for expressway use?
options: Vehicles without headlights, taillights, and brake lights
questions.explanation: The FDM classifies dilapidated and not roadworthy vehicles as those without headlights, taillights, brake lights, vehicles with misaligned chassis, bald tires, etc.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the engine air compressor in heavy and articulated vehicles?
options: To generate compressed air into the system that requires air to operate
To cool the engine during long trips
To provide air conditioning to the cabin
To filter dust from the fuel system
questions.explanation: The FDM states that the primary function of the air compressor is to generate compressed air into the system that requires air to operate.

questions.question: What is the function of the air pressure regulator in the air supply system of heavy vehicles?
options: To regulate the pressure given into the air dryer to avoid unnecessary burst of air pipes and lines
To filter water from the fuel supply
questions.explanation: The FDM states that regulators are required to primarily regulate the pressure given into the air dryer to avoid unnecessary burst of air pipes and lines.

questions.question: What does the air dryer or air purifier remove from the compressed air?
questions.explanation: The FDM states that the air dryer purifies the generated air and removes oil and water substances.

questions.question: What does the four-way valve control in the air supply system of heavy vehicles?
options: The direction of compressed air to serve front and rear brakes, parking brake, and accessories
The flow of coolant through the engine block
The distribution of fuel to each cylinder
The air conditioning output to different cabin zones
questions.explanation: The FDM states the four-way valve controls the direction of compressed air to serve the front and rear brakes, the parking brake and accessories attached to the system.

questions.question: What is stored in the air reservoir tanks of heavy vehicles?
questions.explanation: The FDM states that compressed air are stored on these tanks in the air supply system of heavy and articulated vehicles.

questions.question: What is proactive vehicle maintenance?
options: Performing measures as stated in the service manual based on time or distance traveled
Repairing a vehicle only after it breaks down
Replacing parts only when they fail
questions.explanation: The FDM defines proactive maintenance as performing measures as stated on the service manual of the vehicle where, given a certain period of time or distance travelled, specified parts are due for replacement or service.

questions.question: How does proactive vehicle maintenance differ from preventive maintenance?
options: Proactive follows the service manual schedule, while preventive replaces parts identified during inspection
Proactive repairs after breakdown, while preventive repairs before driving
Proactive only checks tires, while preventive checks the entire vehicle
Proactive is done by the driver, while preventive is done by a mechanic
questions.explanation: The FDM states that preventive maintenance replaces identified parts as a result of inspection to avoid breakdowns, while proactive maintenance performs measures as stated on the service manual.

questions.question: What is corrective maintenance?
options: A procedure where a mechanic performs corrective measures based on findings of preventive maintenance
Maintenance done only on the engine
Checking the tire pressure before every trip
questions.explanation: The FDM defines corrective maintenance as a procedure where a mechanic performs corrective measures or repairs based on the finding of preventive maintenance.

questions.question: What is a probable cause when the engine is not cranking?
questions.explanation: The FDM lists a dead battery as a probable cause when the engine is not cranking, with the remedy being to charge or replace the battery.

questions.question: What might prevent a modern vehicle from starting even if the battery is fully charged?
options: The clutch pedal or brake pedal is not pressed
The air conditioning is turned on
questions.explanation: The FDM states that modern vehicles will not start if the clutch pedal or brake pedal is not pressed.

questions.question: Why might a motorcycle with a carburetor not start on a cold engine?
questions.explanation: The FDM states that on cold engines, motorcycles with a carburetor may not start if not choked.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle rider do with the choke before moving off?
questions.explanation: The FDM instructs motorcycle riders to release the choke before moving off.

questions.question: What is a probable cause when the alternator is not charging?
questions.explanation: The FDM lists loose or broken alternator belt as a probable cause when the alternator is not charging, with the remedy being to tighten or replace it.

questions.question: What is a probable cause when the battery is not charging?
questions.explanation: The FDM lists loose or corroded battery terminals as a probable cause when the battery is not charging, with the remedy being to clean, tighten, or replace.

questions.question: What does abnormal wear on the outer sides of front tires indicate?
questions.explanation: The FDM states that abnormal wear on outer sides of front tires has advanced toe-in as the probable cause, with wheel alignment as the remedy.

questions.question: What does abnormal wear on the inner sides of front tires indicate?
questions.explanation: The FDM states that abnormal wear on the inner sides of front tires has advanced toe-out as the probable cause, with wheel alignment as the remedy.

questions.question: Which set of symptoms indicates camber misalignment?
options: Pulling left or right when driving, noisy steering, and rapid tire wear
Brake squealing and reduced stopping power
questions.explanation: The FDM lists pulling left or right when driving, noisy steering, and rapid tire wear as symptoms of camber misalignment, with the remedy to change tire and adjust camber.

questions.question: Which symptom is indicative of caster misalignment?
options: Poor turning ability of the steering wheel
questions.explanation: The FDM lists poor turning ability of steering wheel as one of the symptoms of caster misalignment, along with pulling to one side when driving and uneven tire wear.

questions.question: What does black or gray smoke from a gasoline engine indicate?
questions.explanation: The FDM states that black or gray smoke from a gasoline engine comes from incomplete fuel combustion, with possible causes including a clogged air filter or malfunctioning carburetor.

questions.question: What does blue smoke from a gasoline engine indicate?
questions.explanation: The FDM states that blue smoke from a gasoline engine indicates engine oil burning, with possible causes including worn out piston rings, valves, or cylinders.

questions.question: Under RA 11235, what is the fine for a motorcycle owner who fails to report a lost, damaged, or stolen motorcycle plate and apply for replacement?
questions.explanation: RA 11235 states the fine for failure to report a lost, damaged, or stolen motorcycle plate is P20,000.00 to P50,000.00.

questions.question: What is the fine for using a stolen number plate or readable number plate on a motorcycle under RA 11235?
questions.explanation: RA 11235 provides a fine of P50,000.00 to P100,000.00 or Prision Mayor, or both, for the use of a stolen or transferred number plate.

questions.question: Under RA 11235, what is the penalty for erasing, tampering, altering, forging, imitating, covering, or concealing a number plate or readable number plate?
options: Fine of P50,000.00 to P100,000.00 or Prision Mayor or both
Fine of P20,000.00 to P50,000.00 and Arresto Mayor
Fine of P100,000.00 to P200,000.00 only
questions.explanation: RA 11235 imposes a fine of P50,000.00 to P100,000.00, Prision Mayor (6 yrs. and 1 day to 20 yrs.), or both.

questions.question: What is the imprisonment penalty for a law enforcer who fails to surrender a seized motorcycle to proper authorities within 24 hours under RA 11235?
options: Arresto Mayor (1 month and 1 day to 6 months)
Prision Correccional (6 months and 1 day to 6 years)
Prision Mayor (6 years and 1 day to 20 years)
Reclusion Temporal (12 years and 1 day to 20 years)
questions.explanation: RA 11235 imposes Prision Correccional (6 months and 1 day to 6 years) on any law enforcer who fails to surrender a seized motorcycle within 24 hours.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is used in the commission of a crime constituting a grave felony under the Revised Penal Code, what is the penalty under RA 11235?
options: Prision Correccional (6 months and 1 day to 6 years)
Prision Mayor (6 years and 1 day to 20 years)
Reclusion Temporal (12 years and 1 day to 20 years) to Reclusion Perpetua
Arresto Mayor (1 month and 1 day to 6 months)
questions.explanation: RA 11235 imposes Reclusion Temporal (12 yrs. and 1 day to 20 yrs.) to Reclusion Perpetua (imprisonment for at least 30 yrs.) when a motorcycle is used in a grave felony.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is used in the commission of a less grave felony or light felony, what is the imprisonment range under RA 11235?
options: Prision Correccional (6 months and 1 day to 6 years) to Prision Mayor (6 years and 1 day to 20 years)
Arresto Mayor (1 month and 1 day to 6 months) only
Reclusion Temporal (12 years and 1 day to 20 years) only
questions.explanation: RA 11235 imposes Prision Correccional (6 months and 1 day to 6 yrs.) to Prision Mayor (6 yrs. and 1 day to 20 yrs.) when a motorcycle is used in a less grave felony or light felony.

questions.question: Under RA 11235, what penalty is imposed if death or serious physical injuries result from the unlawful use of a motorcycle?
options: Prision Mayor (6 years and 1 day to 20 years)
Reclusion Temporal (12 years and 1 day to 20 years)
Reclusion Perpetua (imprisonment for at least 30 years)
Prision Correccional (6 months and 1 day to 6 years)
questions.explanation: RA 11235 imposes Reclusion Perpetua (imprisonment for at least 30 yrs.) if death or serious physical injuries result from the unlawful use of a motorcycle.

questions.question: Under RA 11235, what is the penalty if a seized motorcycle is used in the commission of a crime?
options: Prision Correccional (6 months and 1 day to 6 years)
Maximum penalty of the relevant crime or offense
Prision Mayor (6 years and 1 day to 20 years)
Arresto Mayor (1 month and 1 day to 6 months)
questions.explanation: Under RA 11235, if a seized motorcycle is used in the commission of a crime, the maximum penalty of the relevant crime or offense applies.

questions.question: Under RA 11235, what happens to a motorcycle used in the commission of a crime or offense?
options: It is impounded by the PNP as evidence in custodia legis until termination of the case
It is returned to the owner after 30 days
It is auctioned off to the public
questions.explanation: RA 11235 states a motorcycle used in the commission of a crime shall be impounded by the PNP as evidence in custodia legis until the termination of the case and then forfeited in favor of the government unless the defendant is not guilty or it belongs to an innocent third party.

questions.question: Under RA 11235, what penalty applies when a lost, damaged, or stolen number plate was not reported and the plate was used in a crime?
options: Fine of P20,000.00 to P50,000.00 only
Arresto Mayor (1 month and 1 day to 6 months) to Prision Correccional (6 months and 1 day to 6 years)
Prision Mayor (6 years and 1 day to 20 years)
questions.explanation: For failure to report a lost, damaged, or stolen number plate that was used in a crime, RA 11235 imposes Arresto Mayor (1 month and 1 day to 6 months) to Prision Correccional (6 months and 1 day to 6 yrs.).

questions.question: Under RA 11235, what is the penalty for knowingly selling or buying an erased, tampered, altered, forged, or imitated number plate?
options: Arresto Mayor (1 month and 1 day to 6 months)
Prision Correccional (6 months and 1 day to 6 years)
Prision Mayor (6 years and 1 day to 20 years)
Reclusion Temporal (12 years and 1 day to 20 years)
questions.explanation: RA 11235 imposes Prision Mayor (6 yrs. and 1 day to 20 yrs.) for knowingly selling or buying an erased, tampered, altered, forged, or imitated number plate.

questions.question: Under RA 11235, within how many hours must a lost, damaged, or stolen motorcycle plate be reported to the LTO?
questions.explanation: RA 11235 mandates that the loss of a number plate must be reported to the LTO within 72 hours.

questions.question: What is the fine for driving without a valid driver's license or conductor's permit?
questions.explanation: The fine for driving without a valid driver's license/conductor's permit is Php 3,000.00.

questions.question: For how long is an unlicensed or improperly licensed driver disqualified from being granted a driver's license after driving without a valid license?
questions.explanation: The driver shall be disqualified from being granted a driver's license and driving a motor vehicle for a period of one (1) year from the payment of the fine.

questions.question: What is the fine for driving a motor vehicle used in the commission of a crime upon conviction by a regular court?
questions.explanation: The fine for driving a motor vehicle used in the commission of a crime upon conviction is Php 10,000.00.

questions.question: What happens to the driver's license of a person convicted of using a motor vehicle in the commission of a crime?
options: Confiscated and revoked with perpetual disqualification from being granted a driver's license
Revoked with disqualification for five years
questions.explanation: Upon conviction, the driver's license shall be confiscated and revoked, and the driver shall be perpetually disqualified from being granted a driver's license and driving a motor vehicle.

questions.question: What is the fine for commission of a crime in the course of apprehension upon conviction by a regular court?
questions.explanation: The fine for commission of a crime in the course of apprehension upon conviction is Php 10,000.00.

questions.question: How long is a driver disqualified from being granted a driver's license after conviction for commission of a crime in the course of apprehension?
questions.explanation: The driver shall be disqualified from being granted a driver's license for a period of 5 years counted from the date of payment of appropriate fines and penalties.

questions.question: What is the fine for a first offense of reckless driving?
questions.explanation: The first offense for reckless driving carries a fine of Php 2,000.00.

questions.question: What is the fine for a second offense of reckless driving?
questions.explanation: The second offense for reckless driving carries a fine of Php 3,000.00.

questions.question: What is the fine for a subsequent (third or more) offense of reckless driving?
questions.explanation: The subsequent offense for reckless driving carries a fine of Php 10,000.00.

questions.question: For reckless driving, how long is the driver's license suspended for the second offense?
questions.explanation: For reckless driving, the driver's license shall be suspended for a period of three (3) months for the second offense from payment of fine.

questions.question: For reckless driving, how long is the driver's license suspended for the third offense?
questions.explanation: For reckless driving, the driver's license shall be suspended for a period of six (6) months for the third offense from payment of fine.

questions.question: What happens to a revoked non-professional driver's license for reckless driving?
options: The driver is disqualified from being granted a license for two years
The driver is disqualified from being granted a license for one year
The driver is disqualified from being granted a license for five years
questions.explanation: A revoked non-professional driver shall be disqualified from being granted a driver's license for a period of two (2) years counted from date of revocation.

questions.question: What happens to a revoked professional driver's license for reckless driving?
options: Perpetually disqualified from getting any driver's license
questions.explanation: A revoked professional driver shall be perpetually disqualified from getting any driver's license.

questions.question: What is the fine for submission of fake documents in relation to the application for a driver's license?
questions.explanation: The fine for submission of fake documents in relation to driver's license application is Php 3,000.00.

questions.question: For submitting fake documents in a driver's license application, how long is the driver disqualified from being granted a driver's license?
questions.explanation: The driver shall be disqualified from being granted a driver's license and driving a motor vehicle for a period of one (1) year from the payment of the fine.

questions.question: What is the fine for failure to carry a driver's license, certificate of registration, or official receipt while driving?
questions.explanation: The fine for failure to carry a driver's license, certificate of registration, or official receipt while driving is Php 1,000.00.

questions.question: What is the fine for all other violations of traffic rules and regulations not specifically enumerated?
questions.explanation: The fine for all other violations of traffic rules and regulations is Php 1,000.00.

questions.question: How close to an intersection is parking prohibited under the traffic rules?
questions.explanation: Parking is prohibited within 6 meters of the intersection.

questions.question: How close to a fire hydrant is parking prohibited?
questions.explanation: Parking is prohibited within 4 meters of a fire hydrant.

questions.question: Which of the following is a parking violation under traffic rules?
options: Parking in a designated parking lot
Parking in front of your own garage
questions.explanation: Parking in an intersection is listed as a traffic rule violation.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered a traffic violation under the 'all other violations' category?
questions.explanation: Disregarding traffic signs is listed as a traffic rule violation under the all other violations category.

questions.question: What is the violation called when a driver fails to pass to the right when meeting persons or vehicles coming towards him?
questions.explanation: Driving against traffic is defined as failure to pass to the right when meeting persons or vehicles coming towards him.

questions.question: What constitutes illegal overtaking according to the traffic rules?
options: Failure to pass to the left when overtaking vehicles going the same direction
Failure to pass to the right when overtaking
questions.explanation: Illegal overtaking is defined as failure to pass to the left when overtaking persons or vehicles going to the same direction.

questions.question: What is the violation when a driver increases speed before the overtaking vehicle has completely passed?
questions.explanation: Increasing speed when being overtaken is defined as increasing the speed of the motor vehicle before the overtaking vehicle has completely passed.

questions.question: At what distance ahead must the driver's view be obstructed for overtaking upon a curve to be considered a violation?
questions.explanation: Overtaking upon a curve is a violation when the driver's view is obstructed within a distance of 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: Which of the following is prohibited when approaching the crest of a grade?
questions.explanation: Overtaking upon a crest of a grade is a violation — overtaking or passing another vehicle proceeding in the same direction when approaching the crest of a grade.

questions.question: Is overtaking or passing another vehicle at any railway grade crossing allowed?
options: Yes, if the vehicle is slow
No, it is a traffic violation
questions.explanation: Overtaking at any railway grade crossing is listed as a traffic violation.

questions.question: When is overtaking at an intersection allowed as an exception?
options: When there are no other vehicles
On a highway having two or more lanes for traffic in one direction
questions.explanation: Overtaking at an intersection is prohibited except on a highway having two or more lanes for movement of traffic in one direction where the driver may overtake another vehicle on the right.

questions.question: Which vehicles must be yielded the right of way when operated on official business with audible signals?
options: Ambulance, police, or fire department vehicles
questions.explanation: Failure to yield right of way to ambulance, police or fire department vehicles when operated on official business with audible signals is a violation.

questions.question: What must a driver do before traversing a 'through highway' or railroad crossing?
options: Bring the vehicle to a full stop
questions.explanation: Failure to stop before traversing a 'through highway' or railroad crossing is a violation — the driver must bring the vehicle to a full stop.

questions.question: Which of the following is required when parking a motor vehicle unattended on any highway?
options: Turn off the ignition switch, stop the motor, and notch the handbrake
Put a warning sign behind the vehicle
questions.explanation: Failure to stop motor and notch handbrake when unattended means failure to turn off the ignition switch and stop the motor and notch effectively the handbrake when parking a motor vehicle unattended.

questions.question: Which of the following is a traffic violation related to motorcycle operation?
options: MC carrying more passengers other than the back rider
Driving a motorcycle with a helmet
Carrying a passenger with a helmet
questions.explanation: MC carrying more passengers other than the back rider or cargo other than the saddle bags and luggage carriers is listed as a traffic violation.

questions.question: Is refusal to render service to the public or convey passenger to destination considered a violation?
options: Yes, it is a traffic violation
questions.explanation: Refusal to render service to the public or convey passenger to destination is listed as a traffic violation under the franchise section.
